title: Major Gifts Officer
description:
COMPANY PROFILE

CodeAI is an education innovation nonprofit dedicated to the vision that every student in every school has the opportunity to learn about artificial intelligence (AI) and computer science (CS) as part of their core K-12 education. We increase participation in AI+CS education by reaching students of all backgrounds where they are — at their skill level, in their schools, and in ways that inspire them to keep learning, with a focus on increasing participation by young women and students from other underrepresented groups. The leading provider of K-12 AI+CS education curriculum across the globe, CodeAI also organizes the annual Hour of AI campaign, building on the legacy of the Hour of Code, which has engaged more than 15% of all students in the world!

A unifying approach in a divided world

CodeAI's global role in the K-12 computer science movement is only possible because we use a unifying approach across diverse and often divided stakeholders. At a time of increasing polarization, the idea of increasing opportunity for students unites people from across the political spectrum. CodeAI's team members, students, teachers, and supporters have diverse and diverging view points, and they are all welcome in our mission. Read more.

JOB SUMMARY

CodeAI is looking for a Major Gifts Officer to build a net-new pipeline of high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individual donors and turn those relationships into transformational philanthropic partnerships. Students are already using AI. The question is whether they understand it. Your work funds the digital fluency that lets them understand, direct, question, and create with the technology shaping their lives.

This is a from-scratch prospecting and origination role. You will identify, qualify, cultivate, and independently close new HNW and UHNW donor relationships rather than inheriting a portfolio or working inbound interest. You will own roughly $3M+ in annual fundraising outcomes, with a focus on transformational and multi-year commitments, and you will build the practices that make major giving repeatable at CodeAI.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

In this role, you will:

  • Build a net-new donor pipeline: Identify and develop HNW and UHNW prospects through research, wealth screening, referrals, executive and board networks, events, and direct outreach.
  • Own the full fundraising cycle: Lead prospects from qualification and discovery through cultivation, solicitation, negotiation, and close, with a focus on transformational and multi-year commitments.
  • Deliver revenue outcomes: Own approximately $3M+ in annual fundraising, maintaining pipeline coverage and accurately forecasting progress, risks, and opportunities.
  • Develop cultivation strategies: Create tailored approaches for priority prospects that connect their philanthropic interests to CodeAI's mission, programs, and funding priorities.
  • Partner with executive leadership: Work with the CEO, executives, and board members to open doors and strategically engage leadership in advancing high-potential opportunities.
  • Use events to build and convert pipeline: Design donor experiences that surface new prospects and move existing ones forward.
  • Create compelling donor communications: Develop proposals, pitches, and presentations that connect donor interests to CodeAI's vision and impact.
  • Build scalable prospecting practices: Create repeatable approaches to identification, outreach, qualification, cultivation, and conversion that strengthen CodeAI's major-giving capability.
  • Manage and communicate the pipeline: Maintain accurate prospect and opportunity records in Salesforce, and work across CodeAI to advance opportunities and ensure clean gift processing and stewardship handoffs.

As a secondary focus, you may also identify and cultivate net-new foundation and corporate funding opportunities as they arise.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS

We seek candidates who have:

  • 8+ years of frontline fundraising experience, with significant time in major individual giving and engaging HNW and UHNW individuals.
  • A demonstrated track record of building a major-donor portfolio from the ground up, without relying primarily on an inherited book of business or warm leads.
  • Proven success independently originating, cultivating, and closing six- and seven-figure transformational gifts and multi-year commitments across the full major-gift cycle.
  • Experience owning significant fundraising goals and managing a pipeline capable of producing multi-million-dollar annual revenue, with strong forecasting discipline and experience in Salesforce or a similar CRM.
  • Experience partnering with CEOs, executives, and board members to advance high-value donor relationships.
  • Excellent relationship-building, communication, storytelling, and proposal-development skills, with the judgment and discretion required to engage sophisticated philanthropic investors.
  • A demonstrated ability to operate independently, create opportunity, and deliver results in an ambiguous, high-accountability environment.
  • A deep passion for CodeAI's mission and willingness to travel up to 20% to engage donors and prospects.

We prefer candidates who also have:

  • Experience fundraising in education, technology, AI, or another mission-driven environment.
  • Experience using events and high-touch experiences to originate and cultivate major-donor relationships.
  • Experience developing scalable prospecting and major-giving practices.

In addition, candidates must:

  • Be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident
  • Work within the continental United States
  • Pass a pre-employment background check
  • Be willing to travel up to 20%

OUR CULTURAL PRINCIPLES

The way we work matters as much as the work itself. Before you apply, we invite you to take a look at our cultural principles. They reflect who we are, how we show up for each other, and what we look for in the people who join us.

OUR APPROACH TO AI IN HIRING

At CodeAI, we use AI thoughtfully and responsibly to support human-centered hiring. AI may help with administrative tasks, but every hiring decision is made by real people on our team. We welcome candidates to use AI appropriately in their job search while upholding our values of honesty and integrity throughout the process.

Read our full AI Use Policy in Hiring here.

WHAT IS THE INTERVIEW PROCESS LIKE?

Step 1: Informational Interview - learn more about the role and share your experience (30 minutes)
Step 2a: Interviews with several members of the Code.org team (~3 hours)

Step 2b: Homework

Step 3: Final Panel Interview (1 hour)

Step 4: Reference Checks

All interviews are currently being conducted virtually via Google Meet

TO APPLY

Our team will review all applications on an ongoing basis and if we believe your qualifications would make a great fit, we'll contact you to schedule an informational interview.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS PACKAGE

The expected salary range for this position is $99,000 - $110,000. Most offers are on the lower end of the salary range and are at the company’s sole discretion based on the final candidate’s experience. This allows us to provide a fair and equitable approach to compensation when setting pay and maintaining internal pay equity.

We also offer a comprehensive benefits package for full-time employees that includes:

  • Technology subsidy consistent with our Bring Your Own Device environment
  • Flexible, engaging, and remote working environment
  • Paid time off: 5 weeks total, comprised of 3 weeks vacation annually, plus a 2-week winter break office closure (including Christmas and New Year's), and sick leave
  • Medical, dental and vision premiums paid at 100% for FT positions and their dependents
  • Option to participate in 403b retirement plan
  • Annual professional development stipend
  • The opportunity to help students learn better and change the face of computer science

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

title: Controller
description:
About O.A. Newton

O.A. Newton is a diversified, growing organization with multiple business units serving the agriculture, retail, manufacturing, and material handling, as well as leased properties. The organization is experiencing significant growth and change. This is an exciting opportunity for a financial leader who can quickly understand the business, build strong relationships, and provide meaningful financial insight in a fast-paced environment.

Position Summary

O.A. Newton is seeking an experienced, analytical, and business-minded Controller to lead the organization's financial operations while serving as a strategic financial partner to the President. This is more than a traditional accounting leadership role. The successful candidate will combine strong technical accounting expertise with the business acumen to translate financial information into meaningful insights, recommendations, and decisions.

The Controller will ensure the integrity and effectiveness of the company's accounting and financial operations while proactively identifying trends, risks, opportunities, and ways to improve profitability and cash flow. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable managing the details of financial operations and stepping back to ask, "What are the numbers telling us, and what should we do about it?"

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Financial Leadership

  • Partner directly with the President to support strategic and operational decision-making.
  • Translate financial statements, trends, and data into clear business insights and actionable recommendations.
  • Proactively identify financial risks, opportunities, trends, and emerging issues.
  • Provide financial analysis and scenario modeling to support decisions involving growth, investments, staffing, inventory, pricing, capital expenditures, and operational changes.
  • Help leadership understand the financial impact of operational decisions and identify opportunities to improve profitability, cash flow, and efficiency.
  • Develop meaningful financial and operational KPIs and dashboards that help leadership manage business performance.

Financial Management & Reporting

  • Manage and perform general accounting functions, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, general ledger, reconciliations, journal entries, and month-end close.
  • Prepare and analyze accurate and timely financial reporting for multiple companies/entities.
  • Prepare monthly financial statements by the 10th of the following month.
  • Maintain the integrity and accuracy of the general ledger and balance sheet.
  • Provide clear analysis of financial results, significant variances, trends, risks, and opportunities—not simply historical reporting.
  • Ensure daily reconciliation of bank accounts to general ledger cash accounts.

Cash Flow, Forecasting & Treasury

  • Develop and maintain a rolling 13-week cash flow forecast.
  • Analyze and manage cash inflows, outflows, collections, and expenses and proactively identify potential challenges or opportunities.
  • Evaluate actual performance against forecasts and provide recommendations to leadership.
  • Work with the President to manage banking relationships, credit facilities, debt, and credit line renewals.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cash management and financial efficiency.

Job Costing & Business Performance

  • Manage and improve job costing and work-in-progress accounting.
  • Partner with project managers to increase visibility into project performance, profitability, and cost trends.
  • Develop and monitor KPIs relevant to each business unit.
  • Analyze performance against goals and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Help connect financial results with operational activity so managers can make better business decisions.

Leadership & Process Improvement

  • Build strong relationships with the President and staff across the organization.
  • Communicate financial information clearly and effectively to both financial and non-financial audiences.
  • Lead and develop members of the accounts payable and accounts receivable team.
  • Evaluate and improve accounting, reporting, job-costing, and administrative processes as the organization grows.
  • Learn and effectively utilize the Made2Manage ERP system and improve the flow and accessibility of financial and operational information.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline processes, strengthen controls, improve efficiency, and provide management with better information.
  • Work collaboratively with outside accounting, tax, banking, insurance, and other professional advisors.

Compliance & Administrative Oversight

  • Oversee applicable tax filings, state reporting, and financial compliance requirements.
  • Oversee organizational insurance programs and applicable benefit-related financial responsibilities.
  • Maintain appropriate financial controls and ensure compliance with applicable requirements.

What We're Looking For

O.A. Newton is seeking a Controller who combines technical financial expertise with strong business judgment.

The successful candidate will be:

  • Strategic thinker
  • Analytical problem-solver
  • Proactive
  • Collaborative Leader
  • Strong communicator
  • Adaptable
  • Highly Organized and Detail-Oriented
  • Respectful Influencer

Qualifications & Experience

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 10 years of progressive finance and accounting experience.
  • Demonstrated Controller-level experience with responsibility for financial operations.
  • Strong knowledge of general accounting principles and financial reporting.
  • Experience with cash flow forecasting, financial analysis, and financial modeling.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret financial information and translate it into business recommendations.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with executive and operational leadership.

Preferred:

  • MBA or CPA
  • Experience managing financial operations across multiple business units or entities.
  • Experience with manufacturing, project accounting, job costing, work-in-progress, inventory, or material handling environments.
  • Experience with ERP optimization or financial process improvement.
  • Experience developing executive dashboards and business KPIs.
  • Experience working directly with business owners or executive leadership in a privately held organization.

Physical Requirements

  • This position is primarily office-based and requires the ability to work at a computer for extended periods, including frequent use of a keyboard, mouse, telephone, and other standard office equipment.
  • The Controller must be able to communicate effectively in person, by telephone, and electronically. The position may occasionally require travel between company locations and movement through operational, manufacturing, warehouse, retail, or other business environments.

What Success Looks Like

During the first year, the successful Controller will:

  • Build credibility and strong relationships with the President and leadership team.
  • Develop a strong understanding of each business unit and its financial drivers.
  • Deliver accurate and timely financial reporting.
  • Establish a reliable 13-week cash flow forecasting process.
  • Develop meaningful KPIs and dashboards that leadership uses to manage the business.
  • Become a trusted resource to the President for financial analysis and decision support.
  • Proactively bring forward insights and recommendations that help the organization make better business decisions.

title: Solutions Engineer
description:
About Build

AI for the Built World: Build has created the agentic AI stack for institutional real estate, automating complex development and acquisitions workflows 90% faster than humans to accelerate the world's most important built projects - digital infrastructure, energy, industrial - from concept to completion.

Our mission is to accelerate and amplify the world's most important built projects - inventing a better way to build through a collaboration between human experts and agentic AI. We envision a future where the world's buildings are driven from concept to completion, autonomously. Without delays, cost, and complexity. Enabling people to deliver a magnitude more deals. To make decisions, build relationships and create.

To start, we're partnering with the world's biggest built world institutions from $T alternative assets investors, prolific developers and even governments to push the frontier of what's possible. We're backed by c-suite from Blackstone and OpenAI alongside the world's best venture capital firms.

Join us in shaping the future of the Built World and exponentially accelerate your career in the process. We welcome you to do your life's work here.

About the role

Build's domain experts are the edge of the product. Every hour of their expertise that becomes software is an hour that compounds across every client we serve - and a great deal of that expertise is still trapped in manual, repeated work.

This role sits beside them, in the room, and builds whatever removes it. On a spectrum from infrastructure engineer to customer-facing engineer, you sit at the far customer-facing end: you decide what to build by talking to the person who needs it, you build it, and you own whether it worked.

You are accountable for converting expert judgment into working software, and for the delivery team needing less of its own time to produce more.

You can expect to:

  • Embed with the domain team and learn their work well enough to automate it

  • Build agentic workflows and internal tools that take real work off their plate

  • Ship in front of the user and iterate on what you learn in the room

  • Turn repeated expert judgment into software that holds up in production

  • Own your work end-to-end: design, build, deploy, observe, evolve

  • Bring engineering rigour to workflows that have never had any

  • Feed what you learn back into the core product

  • Decide what is worth building, without waiting for a specification

How to win at Build

Growing Build requires a radically different approach to company building. As a company we're focused on one outcome: winning. That means we move fast, work with intensity, and demand excellence from ourselves. We operate with intensity but create an environment that allows for a lot of fun together. The result is that we're one of the fastest shipping teams in vertical AI, partnering with the best to automate the world around us.

Performance and teamwork are the core of Build's operation. We look for those who are able to do both, who often exhibit a particular ability for;

  • Velocity: You are relentless in asking the right questions to set direction. Once you find the right direction you go all-in.

  • Excellence: You obsess with being the best. For you, excellence is a non-negotiable standard rather than an aspiration.

  • Long time horizons: You choose to be in something for the long run, because that's where most of the returns are realized.

  • Ownership: You take full ownership of the outcomes. You're meticulous in your pursuits and believe you can actively shape your environment rather than adapt to it.

  • Customers: You have a passion for the built world and those who shape it. You probably have a quirky hobby or story that relates to your love for building.

  • Integrity: You chose to do the right thing even when it isn't easy.

  • Trust: You only work with people you can trust because it's the only way to do truly extraordinary things.

  • Yield: You have a burning need to see a result on every action you take and you're always looking for routes to do more with less.

What we offer

  • Radical autonomy, real ownership: High standards. Minimal bureaucracy. You own problems end-to-end, choose how the work gets done, and are accountable for exceptional outcomes. Ownership is matched with meaningful, generous equity.

  • An accelerated founder's track: Build is for builders. If you want to learn what it actually takes to create a generational company - Product judgment, execution speed, and accountability - there is no faster path than building from zero when everything is for grabs.

  • Elite teammates, uncompromising bar: You work with people who think clearly, execute relentlessly, and take full ownership. The team you build becomes the company you build. Growth here is not just professional; it reshapes how you operate and in return how Build operates.

  • Perpetual adventure: We attract the strongest of the strange. Extraordinary experiences are part of the culture - from the food we eat together to the space we occupy. Intensity is intentional.

  • Shape the built world: We are rebuilding how the physical world gets made. Our software doesn't live in the abstract - it turns into real projects breaking ground because we exist. We work with the largest institutions, push the frontier of AI, and watch our decisions translate directly into the world around us.

title: Lead Infrastructure Engineer - Market Data Services
description:
Job Description

Assume a vital position as a key member of a high-performing team that delivers infrastructure and performance excellence. Your role will be instrumental in shaping the future at one of the world's largest and most influential companies.

As a Lead Infrastructure Engineer at JPMorganChase within the Market Data team, you apply deep knowledge of software, applications, and technical processes within the infrastructure engineering discipline. Continue to evolve your technical and cross-functional knowledge outside of your aligned domain of expertise.

The team is responsible for supporting, maintaining, and enhancing a number of critical market data platforms that service multiple lines of business across the firm. We are seeking an experienced individual with a proven history supporting the trading business and its market data needs in a production environment.

Working pattern: This role involves working a shift pattern to cover core trading hours, and some weekend work will be required. The successful candidate will be a strong team player who can also operate with a high degree of autonomy, owning issues end-to-end with minimal supervision when needed.

Job responsibilities

  • Applies technical expertise and problem-solving methodologies to projects of moderate scope and executes creative solutions for design, development, and technical troubleshooting for problems of moderate complexity
  • Provide production support for critical market data platforms, ensuring stability, performance, and availability.
  • Implement production changes and deliver timely resolution to production issues, including clear root-cause ownership and follow-through.
  • Develop tools and automation to improve production support processes, monitoring, and overall stability of the market data infrastructure.
  • Uses enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to accelerate infrastructure analysis and design documentation, validating outputs and handling operational data according to sensitivity and security requirements.
  • Drives a workstream or project consisting of one or more infrastructure engineering technologies and works with other platforms to architect and implement changes required to resolve issues and modernize the organization and technology processes
  • Strongly considers upstream and downstream data and systems or technical implications and advises on mitigation actions

title: Principal Engineer
description:
Help us build an AI-native platform where segmentation, analysis and activation happen through conversation, not configuration.

About the role

This is the most senior individual-contributor engineering role at Lexer. You’ll shape how the engineering organisation builds, through demonstrated technical authority and the quality of the systems you create. You’ll work across every stream, taking on the highest-leverage problems and lifting the standard of engineering around you.

At its core this is a software engineering role. You’re building and operating a SaaS and data platform product that our customers rely on every day — multi-tenant, always-on, and held to a high bar for quality, performance and reliability. Strong software engineering fundamentals are the foundation everything else here is built on.

We’ve transitioned to agentic harness engineering and spec-driven development, where engineers direct AI agents and maintain the systems that produce software rather than writing all of it by hand. You work fluently this way and you push the practice forward, building the guardrails, specifications, and architectural practices that let agents move at speed without eroding the system. We believe good engineering practice matters more in the age of AI, not less: agents amplify whatever system they work in, so clean ones get faster and messy ones get worse. Making ours the kind that compounds is the heart of this role.

Role details

  • Level: Principal Engineer — the most senior individual-contributor role in engineering.
  • Reports to: CTO.
  • Experience: 8+ years of hands-on software engineering, including significant time operating at a senior/staff level across complex systems.
  • Location: Remote or Hybrid Melbourne-based, hybrid — 3 days a week in our St Kilda office, 2 days working from home. We’ll also consider remote candidates with strong, consistent overlap with AEST/AEDT core hours.

How we work

We practice spec-driven development inside an agentic harness: engineers direct AI agents and maintain the systems that produce software. Our engineering culture draws on XP — test-first, continuous integration, small batches, pairing, and shared ownership. This is a hands-on, collaborative role, so being comfortable working closely with others in real time matters as much as working independently.

Our stack

We have a predominantly Python and React stack, running on AWS, with data processing in Databricks. You’ll be equally at home in the data and processing layers as in the interfaces customers touch, and comfortable making architectural decisions that span the whole system.

What you’ll do

  • Work hands-on, in the codebase, across engineering streams on the problems that matter most: the AI capability layer, the data contracts that hold the platform together, and the ongoing modernisation of the platform.
  • Hold architectural direction as a living function rather than a static document, making the calls that keep the system coherent as it changes. You’ll own the ADR process so those calls are captured and understood.
  • Keep the architecture adaptable as the business changes, favouring low coupling, high cohesion, and strong boundaries so the system is resilient, easy to build on, and easy to maintain.
  • Design for reliability and observability from the start, so the platform is dependable and its behaviour is understood.
  • Build the guardrails that keep agentic engineering safe at speed, including spec-driven development, architectural practices, context engineering, and the test coverage that lets agents move fast without breaking things. You’ll push the practice forward across the team.
  • Lift the engineers around you through pairing, code review, and the standard your own work sets.

What success looks like

In your first 3 months

  • You’re hands-on in the team building our new AI flagship product — a strong contributor shipping real product towards PMF, adapting our agentic harness as we go, and running the ADR process.

By 6 months — caretaker of scale

  • As the platform grows, you’re the caretaker of scale — keeping our systems adaptable for new market opportunities and bringing the right amount of rigour and process for our evolving scale, ensuring the infrastructure is fit for purpose.

By 12 months — across the whole platform

  • You work across multiple teams, ensuring the holistic platform works — all the systems fitting together coherently — and you’re recognised as a technical authority who raises the bar across engineering.

What you’ll bring

Must have’s

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, with a track record of building, shipping and operating production SaaS at scale — you care about the craft: clean, well-tested, maintainable code and healthy CI/CD.
  • Deep hands-on engineering across complex systems, ideally with data-intensive or platform work.
  • Practical experience directing AI coding agents to ship production software, and building the guardrails and architectural practices that make it safe at scale.
  • A track record of holding architecture across a whole system, not just a single team.
  • Strong communication. You make complex technical directions clear to engineers and non-engineers alike, and you can model and communicate system designs visually, including with C4.
  • Comfort working in a mature, evolving codebase; you can navigate real complexity and still move fast.
  • Strength across our stack: Python (or similar), React and AWS.

Strong preference

  • Background in CDP, martech, or data platform domains.
  • A foundation in SOLID architectures and XP-style practice — test-first, continuous integration, small batches, shared ownership.

Nice to haves

  • Experience re-platforming legacy stacks toward modern architectures.

title: Systems Administrator

Project Description: FDA.gov website experiences more than 670 million hits, 43.34 TB of data transferred, and 17.4 million visitors per month, making it the "front door" to the FDA for a substantial portion of the public. Support for FDA's web infrastructure, including its Content Management System (CMS), is intended to enhance the agency's ability to manage web content effectively. · Configure and manage Linux and other applicable operating systems, including installs/patching of operating system software, troubleshooting, maintaining

integrity of and configure network components, and implementation of operating systems enhancements to improve reliability and performance

Job Description:

Position Summary

The Vice President of M&A Operations will lead end-to-end operational strategy, due diligence, integration, and separation (carve-out) efforts across the company’s deal pipeline. This role serves as the critical bridge between Corporate Development (deal sourcing/valuation) and Functional Leaders (HR, IT, Product, Sales, Legal, Finance) to ensure acquired businesses are seamlessly integrated and deal value drivers are realized.

3. Executive Governance & Stakeholder Alignment

  • Act as a trusted advisor to C-suite executive sponsors and functional vice presidents, driving consensus and resolving high-level friction points.

title: Staff Fullstack Engineer
description:
About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast — both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.

About the Role

We're building a dedicated growth engineering function at the org level, and this role sits at the center of it. Your mandate is user growth: owning the new user experience from first touch to first trade, reducing friction in the acquisition funnel, and building the surfaces that turn curious visitors into active traders. This is not a siloed frontend or backend job — you will work across the entire stack and cut into whatever territory needs cutting into.

The team operates with a mission-driven structure. You will collaborate closely with product, data, and other engineering teams, but you are expected to drive, not wait. Growth at Polymarket is not a marketing problem — it is an engineering problem. The onboarding flow, the KYC experience, the ad-driven funnels that bring people from a sports broadcast into a live prediction market: all of it gets built here.

What You'll Do

  • Own and iterate on the new user onboarding flow, from account creation through KYC completion, with a focus on activation rates and drop-off reduction

  • Build ad-driven funnel surfaces that route users from external campaigns directly into relevant market pages, coordinating with product on targeting logic and layout

  • Ship fullstack features end to end — writing frontend UI, backend services, and third-party integrations — without needing work parceled out across teams

  • Identify friction points in the user acquisition funnel using product analytics and experiment your way to solutions, measuring impact at each step

  • Review code and make architectural decisions within your domain without waiting for senior sign-off or a fully specced ticket

  • Coordinate across engineering teams to get changes made in services you do not own, aligning stakeholders and keeping things moving

  • Raise the technical bar on the growth team through code review, direct feedback, and helping less senior engineers scope and ship better work

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of fullstack engineering experience, with real depth on both the frontend and backend — not just familiarity with one side

  • Proven track record shipping user onboarding flows, KYC integrations, or acquisition funnel features, with measurable results you can speak to

  • Experience working across teams in a larger engineering org, navigating ownership boundaries and getting things done without top-down coordination

  • Strong product instincts — you can look at a funnel, identify what is broken, and propose a fix without waiting for a product manager to hand you a spec

  • Comfortable making technical tradeoffs at the system level, scoping across frontend, backend, and external services and choosing the right approach for the constraint

  • Clear communicator who can align engineers, product managers, and stakeholders on scope and priorities without creating unnecessary process

  • (Plus) Experience with Web3 onboarding flows or crypto-native KYC and compliance tooling

  • (Plus) Familiarity with prediction markets, financial platforms, or other high-stakes transaction products

  • (Plus) Experience running growth experiments with A/B testing frameworks and interpreting results to drive next steps

Benefits

  • Competitive salary & equity

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage

  • 401k match

  • Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories

title: Athletic Strategy Consultant (Men's/Women's Volleyball)
description:

Crimson students are 7x more likely to get into the Ivy League than their peers. We were recently featured on the front page of the Wall Street Journal.

Crimson is the only college admissions consultancy that brings together:

  • Former Ivy League and Top 20 admissions officers to rigorously review and refine applications

  • Professors and PhD teaching fellows from leading universities to guide students through original, independent research — with pathways to selective peer-reviewed publication or conference presentation

  • Past ISEF winners and judges who coach students to compete for state, national, and international science fair awards

  • Capstone project mentors who help students design and scale leadership initiatives with real-world impact, measurable outcomes, and credible external validation


We’re backed by leading VC firms, including Tiger Global, Heal Partners, IceHouse Ventures, and Movac, and recently closed a USD $40M Series D funding round at a USD $640M valuation. We now operate across 21 markets worldwide, including the US, Canada, UK, Singapore, Japan, Hong Kong, Australia, and New Zealand.

The Role

Crimson Education is currently growing our Global Athletics team and we are looking for a sport-specific Athletic Strategy Consultant (Men's/Women's Volleyball) who has a passion for coaching, mentoring and supporting the next generation of collegiate student-athletes heading to the US. This role will be a contract or part-time job to begin with and fully remote. The work hours and number of clients can be determined by your schedule. There is potential for this role to grow into a full-time position in the future.

What are the main responsibilities for this role?

  • Work closely with student-athletes within your sport who are aiming to play collegiate athletics in the US, developing meaningful mentoring relationships.

  • Consistently meet with each student-athlete through video chat. The expected meeting cadence will be per 2-4 weeks in active recruitment months, and per 3-6 weeks in their earlier years.

  • Maintain consistent communication with student-athletes via our tech platform and through email.

  • Hold student-athletes accountable for organisational and developmental tools, such as training logs and competition reflections.

  • Evaluate film to provide student-athletes with feedback and instruction, as well as suggestions for organising their recruitment video.

  • Research and discuss the best camps/showcases/opportunities for the student-athlete to attend in order to increase their exposure to relevant US college coaches.

  • Help student-athletes maximize their talent using your knowledge and resources to further develop them as athletes.

  • Work with student-athletes to develop a clear, personalized and intentional plan for their US College Athletic recruitment, giving realistic expectations on US school lists.

  • Help student-athletes navigate and stay proactive throughout their recruiting journey.

  • Advocate for student-athletes with US college coaches when appropriate.

  • Update parents on progress of the student-athletes when relevant.

What skills and experience are required?

  • Experience playing and/or coaching at a top US-based university

  • Knowledge of US College and University options (i.e., NCAA D1, D2, D3)

  • Knowledge of SAT/ACT, Academic Requirements, and NCAA Eligibility

  • Detailed understanding of the US College Recruiting process

  • Exceptional emotional intelligence and interpersonal skills

  • Strong strategic planning and communication skills

  • Excellent verbal communication

  • A passion for mentoring teenagers

Why work for Crimson?

  • Rapidly growing start up, with a flexible working environment where you will be empowered to structure how you work

  • Limitless development and exposure - our internal promotions/role changes made up 33% of all recruitment last year

  • $1000 individual training budget per year, we love to ‘Level Up’ (it’s one of our core values)!

  • Psychologist on staff

  • Insightful fireside chats and workshops to help support our high-performing and ambitious team

  • Radical Candor is a feedback approach we live by

  • We’re a global player with 28 markets (and growing) across the globe. Most roles have the option to work from one of our many offices or remotely!

If you're passionate about growing in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and want to work with cutting-edge technology, then we'd love to hear from you!

title: RN Post Op & Oncology Med/Surg FT Days
description:
Your job is more than a job.

Eligible For A Sign On Bonus Up To $15K!!

Why You’ll Love This Role

This is an opportunity to make a difference every single day. You’ll care for patients during critical moments in their recovery and treatment journeys while building meaningful relationships with patients, families, and an interdisciplinary team that shares your commitment to exceptional care.

From celebrating a patient’s recovery after surgery to offering comfort and hope to someone facing a cancer diagnosis, the work you do matters.

You were born to care for others. You bring the clinical skills, heart, resilience, and compassion that make an extraordinary nurse.

Let’s be honest, Post-Op and Oncology nursing is not for everyone. It takes clinical expertise, emotional strength, compassion, and a special ability to care for patients during some of the most vulnerable moments of their lives.

Your calling as an Oncology and Post-Op Nurse is personal. You understand the fragility of life, and when you walk into your patient’s room, you strive to be a ray of sunlight—bringing hope, comfort, reassurance, and exceptional care through pain, recovery, uncertainty, and fear.

On our Post-Op & Oncology Med/Surg Unit, no two days are the same. You’ll care for patients recovering from surgical procedures while also supporting patients throughout their oncology journey. You’ll use your assessment skills, clinical judgment, and nursing expertise to monitor patient conditions, manage complex care needs, prevent complications, and provide compassionate support to both patients and their families.

Your Everyday

  • Take the lead by prioritizing, coordinating, and delegating all aspects of patient care for Post-Op, Oncology, and Med/Surg patients.
  • Provide comprehensive nursing care to patients recovering from surgical procedures and those receiving treatment for oncology-related conditions.
  • Collaborate with physicians, advanced practice providers, case managers, pharmacists, therapists, and other multidisciplinary team members to ensure appropriate, coordinated patient care.
  • Assess, monitor, and respond to changes in patient condition, escalating concerns and implementing appropriate interventions in a timely manner.
  • Manage post-operative care, including pain management, surgical site monitoring, mobility, recovery progression, and prevention of post-operative complications.
  • Support oncology patients and their families by providing compassionate care, education, symptom management, and emotional support throughout their healthcare journey.
  • Maintain and advocate for a safe environment for patients, families, visitors, and fellow team members.
  • Monitor and engage with patients, families, and appropriate care team members regarding significant events, changes in condition, questions, concerns, and ongoing care needs.
  • Prevent and treat wounds while promoting skin integrity and implementing evidence-based interventions.
  • Monitor and execute Joint Commission, infection prevention, and environment of care requirements to maintain a safe and high-quality patient care environment.
  • Ensure continuity of care, efficient patient throughput, consistent communication, and an exceptional experience for every patient and family.
  • Initiate patient and family education using appropriate resources and continuum-of-care services to support recovery, treatment plans, discharge planning, and ongoing healthcare needs.
  • Advise and consult with the supervisor or appropriate leadership when unable to complete assignments or perform tasks promptly, effectively, or safely.
  • Contribute to a collaborative team environment by assisting coworkers and supporting the overall success of the unit—even when you haven’t been asked.
  • Serve as a compassionate advocate for patients and families, ensuring their voices, needs, concerns, and goals remain at the center of care.

The Must-Haves

Minimum Qualifications

Current Registered Nurse license to practice in Louisiana as defined by the Louisiana State Board of Nursing. Current American Heart Association BLS certification. Ability to provide safe, compassionate, and effective nursing care in a fast-paced Post-Op, Oncology, and Medical/Surgical environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN). Minimum of six months of Registered Nurse experience.

Previous experience in Medical/Surgical, Post-Operative, Oncology, or other acute care nursing environments preferred.

WORK SHIFT:

Days (United States of America)

LCMC Health is a community.

Our people make health happen. While our NOLA roots run deep, our branches are the vessels that carry our mission of bringing the best possible care to every person and parish in Louisiana and beyond and put a little more heart and soul into healthcare along the way. Celebrating authenticity, originality, equity, inclusion and a little “come on in” attitude is the foundation of LCMC Health’s culture of everyday extraordinary

Touro

Touro, at the forefront of medical excellence within LCMC Health’s incredible community of care, has been regionally recognized for 165 years as one of New Orleans' most enduring healthcare monuments. It’s where babies come from and New Orleanians are cared for. Learn more about Touro and our Leapfrog “Grade A” Hospital Safety distinction

Your extras

  • Deliver healthcare with heart.
  • Give people a reason to smile.
  • Put a little love in your work.
  • Be honest and real, but with compassion.
  • Bring some lagniappe into everything you do.
  • Forget one-size-fits-all, think one-of-a-kind care.
  • See opportunities, not problems – it’s all about perspective.
  • Cheerlead ideas, differences, and each other.
  • Love what makes you, you - because we do

You are welcome here.

title: Clinical Policy Specialist - Itemized Bill Review (Any city, TX, US, 99999)
description:
It takes great medical minds to create powerful solutions that solve some of healthcare’s most complex challenges. Join us and put your expertise to work in ways you never imagined possible. We know you’ve honed your career in a fast-moving medical environment. While Gainwell operates with a sense of urgency, you’ll have the opportunity to work more flexible hours. And working at Gainwell carries its rewards. You’ll have an incredible opportunity to grow your career in a company that values work-life balance, continuous learning, and career development.

Summary

The Clinical Policy Specialist – Itemized Bill Review is responsible for the development, enhancement, and performance of Itemized Bill Review clinical and coding solutions. This role serves as the primary subject matter expert for Itemized Bill Review policies, methodologies, and audit strategies, leveraging expertise in healthcare reimbursement, facility billing, revenue integrity, coding, payment policies, and regulatory requirements.

The ideal candidate will possess extensive knowledge of inpatient and outpatient facility billing, UB-04 claim processing, itemized bill analysis, coding guidelines, reimbursement methodologies, and payment integrity strategies. This role is responsible for developing and maintaining audit concepts, conducting clinical and coding research, analyzing claims and billing data, monitoring program performance, supporting client implementations, and ensuring content aligns with industry standards and regulatory requirements.

This position plays a critical role in identifying billing vulnerabilities, developing innovative audit strategies, improving claim selection methodologies, and maximizing recovery opportunities while ensuring accurate and defensible review outcomes.

Your role in our mission

  • Collaborate with Medical Directors, Clinical Leadership, Product, Analytics, and Innovation teams to develop clinical, coding, and Itemized Bill Review solutions that enhance audit strategies, claim selection processes, and payment integrity outcomes.
  • Design and implement audit concepts, review criteria, and reimbursement validation strategies to identify billing discrepancies, improve facility billing accuracy, support recovery opportunities, and strengthen payment integrity programs.
  • Leverage data analysis, research, and performance monitoring to develop new clinical and coding concepts, evaluate results, recommend process improvements, and optimize program effectiveness.
  • Monitor changes in clinical and coding guidelines, regulations, and reimbursement policies, updating audit rules and review methodologies to ensure compliance and program alignment.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert for Itemized Bill Review, facility billing practices, reimbursement methodologies, and audit standards, providing guidance to clients, leadership, and cross-functional teams.
  • Develop defensible audit rationales, clinical and coding content, training materials, and documentation while supporting special projects, client discussions, RFP activities, and ongoing program implementation.

What we're looking for

  • Associate’s Degree required, Bachelor's degree preferred (health administration, business, nursing)
  • Active, Unrestricted RN license from the United States and in the primary home residency, active compact multistate unrestricted RN license as defined by the Nurse Licensure Compact (NLC), required
  • At least one of the following coding certifications RHIA, RHIT, CCS, CCS-P, CIC, CPC, CPMA or equivalent clinical/coding credential.
  • 5+ years of experience in payment integrity, healthcare reimbursement, facility claims auditing, medical bill review, DRG validation, revenue integrity, or clinical policy development.
  • 5+ years of experience performing Itemized Bill Review or Medical Bill Review auditing facility claims.
  • 3+ years of experience with healthcare policy, Medicare guidelines and State regulation research and interpretation.
  • Extensive knowledge of Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement methodologies, hospital billing practices, UB-04 claims, coding guidelines, and revenue cycle processes.
  • Experience developing audit concepts, review criteria, policies, or payment integrity solutions.
  • Ability to research State and Federal regulations, clinical policies, coding guidelines to develop and implement policies, clinical/coding resources, and tools to support Gainwell’s Clinical Claim Review products.

What you should expect in this role

  • Location: Remote (U.S.-based)
  • Travel: Up to 10%
  • Employment Type: Full-Time
Applications will be accepted through September 30, 2026.

The pay range for this position is $86,800.00 - $124,000.00 per year, however, the base pay offered may vary depending on geographic region, internal equity, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. Put your passion to work at Gainwell. You’ll have the opportunity to grow your career in a company that values work flexibility, learning, and career development. All salaried, full-time candidates are eligible for our generous, flexible vacation policy, a 401(k) employer match, comprehensive health benefits, and educational assistance. We also have a variety of leadership and technical development academies to help build your skills and capabilities.

We believe nothing is impossible when you bring together people who care deeply about making healthcare work better for everyone. Build your career with Gainwell, an industry leader. You’ll be joining a company where collaboration, innovation, and inclusion fuel our growth. Learn more about Gainwell at our company website and visit our Careers site for all available job role openings.

title: Business Applications/ERP Platform Expert, HR
description:
If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.

Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

"The Platform Expert Engineer – Workday HCM & HR Systems serves as the principal technical authority driving the architectural strategy and continuous evolution of Workday and integrated HR technologies. This role shapes the multi-year platform roadmap by evaluating emerging capabilities, including Workday’s AI features, agentic AI frameworks, and intelligent workflow automation. Partnering with executive leadership, enterprise architects, and HR stakeholders, the expert ensures platform stability, multi-system orchestration, and alignment with enterprise goals.

This position is the primary technical lead responsible for: Strategic Platform Architecture & AI Roadmap, Workday Release Strategy & Testing Governance, Agentic AI & Intelligent Workflow Orchestration, Cross-System Security & Integration Governance, and Executive Stakeholder Engagement.

We are seeking:
- Proven experience driving architectural strategy and technical roadmaps for enterprise HR platforms, specifically Workday HCM, security frameworks, and advanced analytics.
- Expertise in evaluating and operationalizing Workday AI innovations, agentic AI agents, and intelligent automated workflows.
- Strong track record in testing governance, major release management, and cross-system integration across HR, Payroll, and IT environments.

Preferred Qualifications

- Active Workday Pro certifications (e.g., Workday Pro HCM, Workday Pro Security, Workday Pro Reporting, or Workday Pro Integrations) or Workday Integration Architect certification."

This is a Stanford Health Care job.

A Brief Overview
The Applications Platform Expert is a senior individual-contributor role providing deep technical mastery, cross-team solutioning, operational solution impacts and informal leadership within the Applications organization. This role has expertise across a broad healthcare delivery domain, with deeper experience in 1-2 functional technical application areas. This role exists to ensure that the organization's most complex technical, architectural, and solutioning challenges are met with consistent, well-defined expertise that can work across IT functions to examine all available tools and solutions and to bring the right combination to the design. This position is expected to maintain current, authoritative knowledge of the platform's capabilities,(new releases, features, vendor roadmap) and proactively identifies where these should be applied before a challenge or request exists. The Platform Expert operates as a trusted technical authority, a mentor, and a contributor to team and departmental roadmaps, while explicitly deferring people-management, task assignment, and performance-evaluation authority to formal management and project leadership.

Locations
Stanford Health Care

What you will do

  • Technical Solutioning & Tool Evaluation
  • Operates at two deliberate altitudes: high-level solution shaping (options, tradeoffs, rough feasibility) before a project is chartered, and deep technical design once work is initiated. Incumbent should have a familiarity with the existing ecosystem and design solutions that are both fit for purpose and coherent with existing platform and future roadmap alignment.
  • Evaluates build-vs-buy and native-platform-vs-purpose-built tradeoffs on their technical merits, rather than defaulting to whichever platform already has a feature.
  • Maintains working fluency across adjacent IT domains (integration, infrastructure, security, data) sufficient to identify who else needs to be involved in a solution, without owning those domains.
  • Partners with other IT teams as a peer convener — able to run or co-run cross-team solutioning sessions, not simply attend them.
  • Clearly distinguishes the exploratory/advisory solutioning phase from the committed design phase, so early options-generation is not mistaken for a locked decision.
  • Ability to lead and deliver complex organizational level projects serving as the subject matter expert and delivery method decision development
  • Mentoring & Informal Leadership
  • Elevates other analysts' capability through coaching on approach and technique, without owning or evaluating their performance. Provides input and knowledge improvement areas to Application Manager in regards to technical abilities of Analyst I-III roles.
  • Models the standard for quality of build, documentation, and judgment.
  • Is sought out voluntarily by analysts for guidance, reflecting earned credibility rather than assigned authority.
  • Pairs or shadows with less experienced analysts on complex problems to transfer judgment and knowledge, not just answer questions.
  • Surfaces talent and growth signals to people managers as input, rather than making talent decisions directly.
  • Does not conduct performance reviews, does not assign work or set priorities for other analysts by virtue of the role alone, and does not become a default escalation path or accumulate an informal “team.”
  • Direction-Giving on Projects
  • Defines or co-defines the technical approach and build strategy for projects on which they serve as technical expert based on the operational/clinical requirements of the objective. This position also serves as a key build resource on complex projects.
  • Advises on proposed approaches from other analysts, particularly on complex or ambiguous tasks, and serves as peer reviewer on build, configuration, and design.
  • On smaller efforts without a dedicated project manager assigned, may explicitly hold project-coordination responsibilities (sequencing tasks, tracking timeline, assigning work items, completing status reports) as a distinct, named responsibility layered on top of the technical platform expert role.
  • Task and priority authority over other analysts' work exists only when explicitly holding a named PM role designation for that effort and will inform people manager collaboratively — not automatically as a function of technical seniority. Technical authority is over the approach; it is not authority over the individual.
  • Depth & Breadth of Expertise
  • Maintains implementation-level, hands-on fluency (current, not historical) in one to two defined domains of true mastery. Viewed as an informal escalation point for platform questions.
  • Maintains working (not mastery-level) fluency across adjacent systems and integration points connected to their core depth area, sufficient to be a solutioning-partner with other teams.
  • Domain depth and adjacent breadth are defined by the role and validated through hiring and periodic leveling review, rather than from individual tenure or interest.
  • Documentation & Staying Current
  • Documents build decisions and their rationale so institutional reasoning survives staff turnover, and keeps documentation current as systems evolve, utilizing Service Now knowledge base or other leadership approved knowledge repositories that retain versioning.
  • Writes documentation for future readers who were not present for the original decision, and proactively transfers knowledge rather than becoming a single point of knowledge failure.
  • Maintains awareness of industry trends, major vendors, and shifts in the vendor landscape within their assigned domain, using that knowledge to inform documentation, solution recommendations, and roadmap input.
  • Documents vendor roadmaps and emerging technology in their domain, bringing forward potentially relevant tools or approaches unprompted, with a clear point of view distinguishing genuine capability from vendor hype.
  • Roadmap Contribution
  • Provides technical input to managers developing domain or team roadmaps, grounded in vendor release schedules, upcoming features, and emerging trends. Surfaces developments that should factor into prioritization decisions, such as an upcoming platform feature that changes a build-vs-buy calculus, or future feature releases that may impact sequencing.
  • Provides application upgrade maintenance schedule recommendations and cost forecast from vendor roadmap.
  • Proactively seeks opportunities for application rationalization as the features of the domain applications evolve and overlap and brings these opportunities to appropriate managers overseeing these applications.
  • Input is advisory: the manager retains ownership of roadmap decisions, sequencing, and resourcing. The Expert ensures the roadmap is technically informed.
  • AI and AI Tools
  • Uses AI tools actively in their own work (build, testing, documentation, troubleshooting) and models effective, appropriately-verified use for others.
  • Evaluates AI-powered tools and solutions as part of technical solutioning, including build-vs-buy and native-platform-vs-purpose-built tradeoffs, assessing real capability and fit against actual workflow and data.
  • Considers AI-specific risk dimensions (where human review remains required, where errors are costly) as part of any recommendation.
  • Feeds AI-specific technology awareness into the roadmap contribution function, flagging where emerging AI capability should influence a manager's prioritization.
  • Provides recommendation for data foundation required to safely execute AI model deployment and associated operational workflow gaps that may drive errors in AI deployment.
  • Actively helps define monitoring plans for AI-enabled applications, including what should be monitored, acceptable thresholds, review points, escalation paths, and operational gaps or risks that need management attention. The role guides the monitoring design based on technical expertise, but does not need to own day-to-day monitoring unless explicitly assigned.
  • Other Modeled Behaviors
  • Demonstrates composure and clarity under ambiguity, transparency about tradeoffs, and openness to challenge on their own technical judgment.
  • Independently follows through reliably on commitments to advise or investigate, and demonstrates calibrated confidence — comfortable acknowledging the limits of their own expertise.
  • Escalates and discusses platform issues to leaders with recommended resolution and prioritization based on severity.


Education Qualifications

  • Bachelors degree in a relevant field (Information Systems, Computer Science, Health Informatics, Health Management, or related) is required.


Experience Qualifications

  • 8+ years of progressively responsible experience in healthcare applications/IT, including demonstrated hands-on build and configuration experience in one or more core systems (Epic, Workday, Sectra, or other related application)
  • Demonstrated track record of resolving complex, escalated problems that others have been unable to close, with measurable delivery outcomes.
  • Experience partnering across multiple IT teams or portfolio verticals on solution design, without formal authority over those teams.
  • Experience mentoring or informally coaching less experienced staff, without formal people-management responsibility.


Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Implementation-level, current fluency in one to two defined technical domains, with working fluency across adjacent, connected systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate and recommend technical solutions and design configuration (including build-vs-buy and platform-native-vs-purpose-built tradeoffs) based on solution merit rather than default.
  • Strong coaching and communication skills, with the judgment to influence without formal authority.
  • Clear judgment regarding when a decision is theirs to make versus when it requires escalation to management or governance.
  • Strong documentation discipline and habits that support knowledge transfer and incorporation into AI tools.
  • Working knowledge of AI-enabled tools relevant to their domain, including the ability to evaluate them critically for real-world fit and monitoring methods.
  • Ability to demonstrate continuing education to remain relevant within associated domain and industry direction.


Preferred Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Prior experience acting as a technical lead or informal project coordinator on smaller initiatives without a dedicated project manager.
  • Experience contributing technical input to departmental or team roadmap planning.
  • Familiarity with evaluating AI/automation solutions in a healthcare or enterprise IT context.

You will work closely with:

You will manage projects throughout their full lifecycle, from initial discovery and planning through execution, release, client acceptance, and closure. You will be accountable for keeping projects within the agreed scope, budget, timeline, resource, and quality expectations.

The role goes beyond traditional project coordination. You will work directly with client stakeholders to clarify business needs, transform them into clear and testable requirements, and maintain the product backlog when no dedicated Business Analyst is available.

You will also stay close to the client’s wider business context, identify risks and improvement opportunities, support pre-sales and estimation activities, and recognise areas where GT may be able to provide additional value.

title: Member of Technical Staff, AI-Driven Compilation
description:
At SF Tensor, we're building the future of high-performance compute

We firmly believe that the future of AI depends on the unglamorous: rethinking and rebuilding the stack, all the way down. From the hardware underneath it to the compiler targeting it and the cloud running it. Right now those three things fight each other and that friction shows up as a tax on every researcher trying to build something ambitious. We're here to axe that tax and make compute faster, cheaper and more available. When we succeed, compute will be portable enough that "which cloud, which chip" stop being something you worry about.

To achieve this, we are building our Kernel Optimizer, which takes code and finds its fastest possible form for whatever vendor and cluster topology you point it at, automatically, as well as the Model Foundry which manages the runs, makes research easier and moves workloads across clouds and chips as prices and availability ship, instead of leaving you locked into whatever vendor you signed with first.

We're backed by Susa Ventures, Y Combinator, along with some great funds and angels including Max Mullen and Paul Graham, as well as founders and executives at Neuralink, Notion and AMD. We're looking for researchers, engineers and organizations who agree with the basic premise: you don't get the next leap in AI without a leap in compute first.

About the Role

We build the fastest GPU compiler in the world. Most compilers have to preserve correctness at every transform, constraining how far they can search, while we prove correctness at the end instead, allowing us to search a far wider space, with agents, with RL, with anything that works and still guarantee the result. It's why we hold #1 on NVIDIA's own kernel benchmark across hundreds of production kernels.

We're hiring a Member of Technical Staff for AI-Driven Compilation to own the search itself. Proving correctness at the end is what makes the search legal and your job is to make it good.

You'll be building the agentic and RL systems that decide which programs are worth trying (instruction selection, scheduling, barriers and stall counts, tiling, fusion, phase ordering) over a space that is enormous precisely because nothing in it has to be conservative.

The reward signal here is unusually clean for RL: measure wall-clock on real silicon gated by a formal proof. No proxy metrics, no reward hacking that survives contact with the verifier. The system already does things worth seeing. Given only a naive attention spec, the search found FlashAttention v4-level performance on a B300 in about 25 minutes, but it also generalizes. The same loop runs on AMD, TPU and Trainium as well as targets we'd never seen before, such as Apple Silicon.

You'll have access to better tooling than anywhere else because we own the stack all the way down to the ISA, allowing us to create kernels that others can't even express. For example, our custom LLVM backend emits cubins directly, without ptxas, letting us work on instruction selection, scheduling, register allocation and stall counts. Our team understands the hardware better than anyone else, to this extent we've built a bit-exact software model of Blackwell's tcgen05.

The kernels you create will ship immediately on runs such as pre-training AlphaFold v3 at 3.4× the throughput, post-training robotics models on Trainium or running our custom RL rollout engine on TPU at multi-100B parameter scale.

What You'll Do

  • You'll design and implement RL systems that search over a massive program space: instruction selection, schedules, tile sizes, fusion strategies and phase ordering

  • You'll build agentic compilation loops that use LLMs to reason about IR, propose transformations and learn from measured results

  • You'll design the search and credit-assignment machinery around an exact reward built from measured latency on real hardware and a formal correctness proof

  • You'll create representations and embeddings of compiler IR that hold up under learned optimization

  • You'll build the training infrastructure for compiler optimization agents, including rollout throughput and distributed evaluation on real silicon

  • You'll push transfer and cold-start performance so that the search works on unfamiliar targets and new ISAs from the first trial

  • You'll close the loop with production workloads so that the compiler keeps improving from what customers actually run

  • You'll work directly with our compiler and kernel engineers to land learned components in the shipping pipeline

  • You'll run rigorous experiments, dig into the results, iterate on them and publish or open-source some of them

What We're Looking For

  • Someone with a strong background in reinforcement learning with hands-on experience training agents

  • Someone with experience building LLM agents, tool use and other agentic systems

  • Someone with familiarity in GPU programming concepts and a willingness to get down to the ISA

  • Someone proficient in PyTorch or JAX

  • Someone with the ability to design and run experiments that produce trustworthy results

Nice to Have

  • Someone with experience in ML compiler stacks (XLA, TVM, Triton, MLIR) or LLVM backends

  • Someone with a background in program synthesis, superoptimization, combinatorial search, formal methods, SMT solvers or verified compilation

  • Someone familiar with RLHF, reward modeling or preference learning

  • Someone with research contributions in RL or learned optimization

  • Someone familiar with GPU performance optimization, profiling and microbenchmarking

Why Join Us

Compiler optimization is the rare place where a learned system gets an enormous action space and a ground-truth reward at the same time. What usually blocks this work is everything around it (a background that can't execute what the search finds or no way to trust the result). You get both here: direct cubin emission below ptxas and a prover that tells you whether the program is correct. In this role, you'll have the tools and researches to let your most ambitious research ideas run wild and if they find valid kernels, ship them into production in days rather than becoming a paper and then nothing.

We're a small team operating at frontier scale. We pre-trained foundation models on 4,000 AMD GPUs as a team of three, designed and brought up GB300 NVL72 clusters and designed a TOP500 supercomputer.

We believe that hard problems get solved in person and most of our work happens at our office in San Francisco. We offer relocation assistance and, where possible, we'd like you here as often as possible.

The base salary range for this full-time position is $275,000-$315,000, plus meaningful equity and benefits.

description:

As a Senior Cloud Data Engineer, you’ll be hands-on across both cloud infrastructure and data engineering, helping shape and deliver our Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and analytics capabilities.

  • Contribute to the design and evolution of the GCP cloud platform and data engineering architecture.

  • Help define, uplift, and embed engineering standards across infrastructure, data pipelines, data models, and development practices.
  • Design, build, and maintain GCP infrastructure including IAM, resource hierarchy, networking, and environments using Terraform or similar IaC tools.
  • Design, build, and maintain data transformation pipelines and analytical data models using Dataform, dbt, or equivalent frameworks on BigQuery.

Ideally you’ll also have:

  • A bachelor’s qualification in Information Technology or a related field.
  • Strong experience designing and implementing cloud platform services such as IAM, environments, networking, and resource hierarchy (GCP experience highly regarded).
  • Strong data engineering experience, including data warehousing, dimensional modelling, and ELT/ETL patterns.
  • Practical production experience with BigQuery or a comparable cloud-native data warehouse.
  • Experience using Infrastructure as Code (Terraform preferred).
