title: UG Ventilation Specialist – RoW
description:
UG Ventilation Specialist – RoW

Position Description

The Barrick RoW Team are seeking to recruit an UG Ventilation Specialist – RoW.

The UG Ventilation Specialist – RoW is a regional technical specialist responsible for providing expert underground ventilation support, governance and capability building across multiple mine sites in RoW. The role will work closely with site and regional teams to standardise ventilation practices, improve operational performance and ensure safe, compliant and efficient underground mining operations.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Actively encourage, motivate and demonstrate a culture of safety leadership.
  • Provide assistance and expertise with the RoW UG Mining Management Operating System (MOS):
    • Regional operational oversight to ensure a standardised approach to mine ventilation occurs that is considered industry best practice.
    • Ensure underground mine plans capture, quantify and escalate where changes/variations are required
    • Identification of any risks and opportunities that exist in the mining schedule
  • Build technical capability and standards
    • Develop regional ventilation standards and best practices and establish bi-weekly RoW ventilation review board.
    • Provide Technical upskilling, training and guidance for team members where suitable
    • Standardise software requirements through the use of the available VentSim packages.
  • Align site activities to the business plan and broader business goals
    • Provide governance for all UG operations that are realistic and achievable.
    • Ensure execution of the agreed mining plan by operational teams in a safe, efficient and timely manner.
    • Review, assess and drive operational performance improvements.
    • Explore development opportunities.
    • Assist in developing short-term budgets and cash flow forecasts for the region.
  • Manage the operational performance of sites
    • Provide technical guidance to the site and regional teams, spending time on ground and engaging regularly to track progress.
    • Ensure optimal performance of underground operations whilst proactively addressing and overcoming potential obstacles.
    • Provide guidance and direction to capital infrastructure projects.
    • Promote safety standards across all operations, including contractors on site, in line with Barrick’s Journey to Zero Harm.
  • Develop the capability of site leadership teams
    • Build a relationship of trust and respect, and proactively performance manage with feedback and interventions to drive individual and team performance.
    • Provide career growth opportunities for leaders and ensure adequate succession planning is in place.
    • Support and mentor technical, professional and leadership development for operational based employees
  • Act as a key interface between ExCo and underground sites
    • Update the RoW ExCo as required, distilling important information and reporting on the sites’ UG technical performance against the business plan, including key challenges and necessary actions.
  • Build and maintain Barrick’s License to Operate
    • Working closely with key site personnel to drive engagements with host nation stakeholders, such as government agencies, local communities, and suppliers.
    • Ensure awareness of differing requirements across all sites.
    • Play a key role in the localisation of the workforce, bringing nationals through and managing their careers.
  • Lead regional ventilation governance and assurance
    • Conduct periodic site ventilation reviews, audits and gap assessments across RoW underground operations.
    • Track ventilation compliance against internal standards, regulatory requirements, life-of-mine plans and operational risk controls.
    • Develop and maintain a regional ventilation risk register, including key controls, corrective actions and follow-up plans.
  • Own regional ventilation modelling standards
    • Establish minimum requirements for ventilation modelling, scenario planning, data quality and model updates across sites.
    • Review VentSim models and ventilation assumptions used in mine plans, production schedules, capital projects and feasibility studies.
    • Support ventilation trade-off studies for mine expansions, production ramp-ups, infrastructure changes and new mining areas.
  • Support short-, medium- and long-term mine planning
    • Ensure ventilation designs are integrated into mine planning, sequencing, development schedules and production forecasts.
    • Review ventilation capacity requirements against future production profiles and equipment fleets.
    • Identify ventilation constraints that may impact production delivery, safety, heat load, airflow, diesel particulate exposure or emergency response readiness

Qualification Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mining Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
  • Postgraduate qualification, professional certification or specialised training in mine ventilation or a related field would be advantageous.
  • Professional registration with a recognised engineering or mining authority would be advantageous.


Experience and Skills Requirements

  • Minimum 10 years’ underground mine ventilation experience, ideally gained in mechanised hard-rock mining environments.
  • Demonstrated experience providing technical ventilation support across multiple underground mine sites, preferably in a regional, group or corporate specialist capacity.
  • Strong practical experience in the design, implementation, review and optimisation of primary and secondary underground ventilation systems.
  • Advanced ventilation modelling capability, including experience using VentSim or similar mine ventilation software to support scenario analysis, mine planning and operational decision-making.
  • Sound knowledge of underground ventilation standards, statutory requirements, occupational hygiene principles, air quality management, heat stress, dust and gas control, and emergency preparedness requirements.
  • Experience developing standards, guidelines, audit frameworks, technical reports and improvement plans for underground ventilation systems.
  • Proven ability to influence, coach and build capability in site-based technical and operational teams without direct line authority.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to communicate technical risks, recommendations and performance insights to site leadership, regional teams and senior executives.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly across RoW to support site reviews, audits, projects and capability-building activities.

What We Can Offer You

  • A comprehensive compensation package including bonuses and site-specific benefits
  • The ability to make a difference and lasting impact
  • Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
  • Opportunities to grow and learn with the industry colleagues are endless
  • Access to a variety of career opportunities across the organization

We are committed to a safe work environment sending every person home safe and healthy every day and leaving a sustainable legacy on our host communities.

  • Experiencia en entornos corporativos globales o de servicios compartidos.
  • Conocimiento de procesos de auditoría y controles internos.
  • Nivel intermedio de inglés para interactuar con equipos regionales o globales.
  • Experiencia participando en proyectos de mejora continua o automatización de procesos.

En DXC encontrarás una cultura de colaboración, aprendizaje continuo y crecimiento profesional. Promovemos un ambiente inclusivo donde cada persona puede desarrollar su potencial mientras contribuye al éxito de nuestros clientes y de nuestra organización.

title: Senior Associate - Secured Risk
description:
Sr Associate - Sec Risk Analytics

About Credit Saison

Established in 2019, Credit Saison India (CS India) is one of the country’s fastest growing Non-Bank Financial Company (NBFC) lenders, with verticals in wholesale, direct lending and tech-enabled partnerships with Non-Bank Financial Companies (NBFCs) and fintechs. Its tech-enabled model coupled with underwriting capability facilitates lending at scale, meeting India’s huge gap for credit, especially with underserved and under penetrated segments of the population.

Credit Saison India is committed to growing as a lender and evolving its offerings in India for the long-term for MSMEs, households, individuals and more. Credit Saison India is registered with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and has an AAA rating from CRISIL (a subsidiary of S&P Global) and CARE Ratings.

Currently, Credit Saison India has a branch network of 80+ physical offices, 2.06 million active loans, an AUM of over US$2B and an employee base of about 1,400 employees. Credit Saison India is part of Saison International, a global financial company with a mission to bring people, partners and technology together, creating resilient and innovative financial solutions for positive impact. Across its business arms of lending and corporate venture capital, Saison International is committed to being a transformative partner in creating opportunities and enabling the dreams of people.

Saison International is the international headquarters (IHQ) of Credit Saison Company Limited, founded in 1951 and one of Japan’s largest lending conglomerates with over 70 years of history and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. The Company has evolved from a credit-card issuer to a diversified financial services provider across payments, leasing, finance, real estate and entertainment. Based in Singapore, Saison International’s global operations span over Singapore, India, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Mexico, Brazil, with active investments in debt, equity, corporate venture capital, and technology.

About The Role:

This critical role acts as a bridge between technical modeling and business execution. The successful candidate will perform micro-level portfolio analysis, track emerging delinquency patterns, and formulate credit risk strategies. By partnering with Data Science, Product, and Engineering teams, the role ensures that predictive risk models and alternative data streams are optimally deployed to drive safe, profitable asset growth across various secured lending products.

Core Responsibilities:

  • Portfolio Analytics & Delinquency Tracking: Conduct continuous, granular portfolio analytics and monitor delinquency trends at a micro-level. Identify and isolate performance indicators across distinct segments, to isolate risk drivers and spot growth opportunities.

  • Lifecycle Credit Strategy Development: Lead the creation, evaluation, and refinement of data-driven credit strategies across the entire customer lifecycle, including automated customer acquisition, portfolio limit management, fraud containment, and automated collection triggers.

  • Trend Identification & Reporting: Uncover underlying portfolio behaviors and macro trends by executing complex data cuts and rigorous statistical validation, delivering actionable risk intelligence to support internal and leadership portfolio reviews.

  • Cross-Functional Strategy Implementation: Collaborate extensively with the Product and Engineering teams to map out risk strategies, policy rules, and decisioning workflows, ensuring seamless implementation into the production environment.

  • Model Optimization & Score Cut-Offs: Partner directly with the Data Science team to provide crucial domain expertise on key model variables, validate predictive performance, and dynamically optimize score-card cut-offs for various proprietary risk models.

  • Data Source Evolution & Alternative Underwriting: Develop an exhaustive knowledge of traditional (credit bureau) and alternative/digital data streams. Innovate optimal configurations for incorporating these diverse sources to enhance predictive accuracy.

  • Product Architecture Alignment: Maintain a robust functional understanding of secured lending products (e.g., Home Loan, LAP in both prime and affordable segment) to ensure risk frameworks perfectly align with business margins and product design.

Key Requirements:

  • Educational Background: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or a highly quantitative discipline from a premier institution

  • Professional Experience: 5+ years of professional experience within Data Science, Risk Analytics, or Quantitative Risk Management. Proven experience building predictive models, optimizing credit policies, and delivering complex analytical insights.

  • Technical & Tool Proficiency: Advanced mastery of SQL for complex data extraction, querying, and manipulation. Strong hands-on programming proficiency in Python or R for statistical analysis and machine learning.

  • Statistical Expertise: Deep conceptual and practical understanding of advanced statistical foundations, including descriptive analytics, experimental design, hypothesis testing, Bayesian inference, confidence intervals, and probability distributions.

  • Machine Learning & Data Mining: Proficiency with core machine learning techniques and statistical algorithms, specifically decision tree learning, ensemble methods (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting), logistic regression, and cluster analysis.

  • Data Dexterity: Demonstrated competence in processing, clean-up, and engineering of large-scale datasets, with a proven ability to work with both highly structured financial databases and semi-structured/unstructured data sources.

  • Domain Expertise: Deep functional knowledge of retail credit lines, secured credit products. Exposure to Fintech lending ecosystems, retail banking, NBFC operations, or SME/LAP/Secured lending is strongly preferred.

title: Engineering Lead
description:
About KIRA

Our mission is to make money smart, reliable and within reach for everyone.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in Asia and it includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and at ease and self reliance, become an expert. We believe AI will help us achieve this in our generation.

Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

KIRA builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Engineering Lead owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems. This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

What You'll Own

  • Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

  • Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

  • Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

  • Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

  • Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

  • Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

Nice to have

  • Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Growth Engineer
description:
About Build

AI for the Built World: Build has created the agentic AI stack for institutional real estate, automating complex development and acquisitions workflows 90% faster than humans to accelerate the world’s most important built projects - digital infrastructure, energy, industrial - from concept to completion.

Our mission is to accelerate and amplify the world's most important built projects - inventing a better way to build through a collaboration between human experts and agentic AI. We envision a future where the world's buildings are driven from concept to completion, autonomously. Without delays, cost, and complexity. Enabling people to deliver a magnitude more deals. To make decisions, build relationships and create.

To start, we're partnering with the world's biggest built world institutions from $T alternative assets investors, prolific developers and even governments to push the frontier of what's possible. We’re backed by c-suite from Blackstone and OpenAI alongside the world’s best venture capital firms.

Join us in shaping the future of the Built World and exponentially accelerate your career in the process. We welcome you to do your life's work here.

About the role

This role exists to remove constraints on Build’s growth and to manufacture upside where it should not reasonably exist. You provide judgment, problem solving, and commercial aggression. The role is obsessed with top line outcomes and treats anything slowing growth or creating asymmetric opportunity as a problem to be engineered away. This role carries direct accountability for growth rate and revenue acceleration.

You are accountable for identifying, prioritising, and eliminating the biggest impediments to Build’s growth while engineering disproportionate top line results from finite effort.

You can expect to:

  • Build outbound systems that find and qualify the right people before they find us

  • Own how Build is discovered - search, content, LLM answers, programmatic surfaces

  • Design and run growth experiments: form the hypothesis, build it, read the data, kill it or scale it

  • Create a system around company communications that compounds - case studies, thought leadership, technical posts, things that travel

  • Invent distribution plays that other companies have not tried yet - referral loops, physical stunts, partnerships, events

  • Build and manage the tools that make inbound work without constant human input

  • Stand up the analytics that make growth legible and hold the team to what they show

  • Work directly with the founding team on what to try next and why

The individual we're looking for is someone with chips on their shoulder and something to prove. A sign of this is that you want to found after you make it big at Build.

How to win at Build

Growing Build requires a radically different approach to company building. As a company we’re focused on one outcome: winning. That means we move fast, work with intensity, and demand excellence from ourselves. We operate with intensity but create an environment that allows for a lot of fun together. The result is that we're one of the fastest shipping teams in vertical AI, partnering with the best to automate the world around us.

Performance and teamwork are the core of Build’s operation. We look for those who are able to do both, who often exhibit a particular ability for;

  • Velocity: You are relentless in asking the right questions to set direction. Once you find the right direction you go all-in.

  • Excellence: You obsess with being the best. For you, excellence is a non-negotiable standard rather than an aspiration.

  • Long time horizons: You choose to be in something for the long run, because that’s where most of the returns are realized.

  • Ownership: You take full ownership of the outcomes. You’re meticulous in your pursuits and believe you can actively shape your environment rather than adapt to it.

  • Customers: You have a passion for the built world and those who shape it. You probably have a quirky hobby or story that relates to your love for building.

  • Integrity: You chose to do the right thing even when it isn’t easy.

  • Trust: You only work with people you can trust because it’s the only way to do truly extraordinary things.

  • Yield: You have a burning need to see a result on every action you take and you’re always looking for routes to do more with less.

What we offer

  • Radical autonomy, real ownership: High standards. Minimal bureaucracy. You own problems end-to-end, choose how the work gets done, and are accountable for exceptional outcomes. Ownership is matched with meaningful, generous equity.

  • An accelerated founder’s track: Build is for builders. If you want to learn what it actually takes to create a generational company – Product judgment, execution speed, and accountability – there is no faster path than building from zero when everything is for grabs.

  • Elite teammates, uncompromising bar: You work with people who think clearly, execute relentlessly, and take full ownership. The team you build becomes the company you build. Growth here is not just professional; it reshapes how you operate and in return how Build operates.

  • Perpetual adventure: We attract the strongest of the strange. Extraordinary experiences are part of the culture - from the food we eat together to the space we occupy. Intensity is intentional.

  • Shape the built world: We are rebuilding how the physical world gets made. Our software doesn’t live in the abstract - it turns into real projects breaking ground because we exist. We work with the largest institutions, push the frontier of AI, and watch our decisions translate directly into the world around us.

    • Architect, build, and maintain highly scalable, secure, and automated CI/CD pipelines tailored for an enterprise Kubernetes ecosystem.

    • Experience integrating security and compliance checks into automated pipelines (DevSecOps).
    • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to drive architectural consensus across engineering teams.

title: Head of IT Service Delivery and Experience
description:
Salary: $180,000 - $200,000 + superannuation

This isn't a turnaround.

Most senior technology service leaders are hired because something is broken.

This isn't one of those opportunities.

Our client already has a technology service known for being responsive, accessible and highly connected to the people it supports. The opportunity is to preserve those strengths while bringing greater consistency, visibility and maturity to how the function operates.

As Head of Service Delivery & Experience, you'll lead a multidisciplinary team spanning frontline technology services, Modern Workplace engineering and training and adoption.

This is broader than a traditional Service Delivery Manager role. You'll influence not only how technology support is delivered, but the underlying workplace technology creating that experience.

What you'll be doing

A major focus will be progressing the function through a clear maturity path: Service → Self-Service → Automation.

Great human service remains the foundation. From there, you'll make it easier for people to resolve straightforward issues through better knowledge and self-service, while identifying predictable activity that can ultimately be automated.

You'll strengthen ITSM practices across incident, request, problem and change management, while improving how service interactions are captured and measured. Data and customer feedback will help identify recurring problems and where improvement will have the greatest impact.

Modern Workplace also sits within your portfolio. You'll lead across Microsoft 365, endpoints, identity and productivity technologies, with priorities including Teams and SharePoint adoption, asset management and continued modernisation of the end-user environment.

You'll work alongside specialist leaders across infrastructure, cyber security, applications and data to address underlying issues rather than simply manage the demand they create.

A different kind of service environment

Technology support in education is immediate and highly visible.

Teachers may need assistance while delivering a lesson. Students arrive with devices. During assessments, a technology issue can quickly affect someone's ability to teach, learn or work.

Good service therefore requires more than processes and ticket metrics. Relationships, responsiveness and judgement matter.

Ultimately, technology should enable the experience without getting in the way. Teachers should be able to teach, students should be able to learn and staff should be able to focus on their work.

The leadership opportunity

You'll inherit a capable team rather than needing to rebuild one.

Your role is to develop that capability through coaching, clearer expectations and greater ownership. Success isn't becoming the permanent escalation point. It's creating a team with the confidence and autonomy to make good decisions and continuously improve the service.

Technical capability matters. During significant incidents or complex issues, you'll need to troubleshoot problems, challenge technical thinking and help the team work towards resolution.

You don't need to be the deepest specialist across every platform, but you do need enough practical depth to independently work through complex issues and recognise when specialist escalation is required.

Who you'll do it for

Our client is a highly regarded organisation in the education sector, combining the scale and technology investment of a large organisation with a much more personal environment.

Technology is well supported, with specialist leadership across infrastructure, cyber security, applications and data. You'll work closely with an experienced CIO as part of a broader technology leadership team, providing exposure and development that can be difficult to find when you're carrying an entire technology function yourself.

The culture is warm, collegiate and highly people-focused, with technology closely connected to the community it supports.

The role is based on Sydney's Upper North Shore and is five days onsite, with ad-hoc flexibility when required. Street parking is readily available nearby.

Remuneration is $180,000–$200,000 base salary + superannuation.

What you'll need

There are two backgrounds that could work particularly well.

You might be an IT Director or technology leader within a smaller school, not-for-profit or similar organisation. You're used to wearing multiple hats but particularly passionate about service excellence and people leadership. You're now ready for greater scale, specialist peers and the opportunity to focus on the part of technology leadership you enjoy most.

Alternatively, you may be a Head of Service Delivery, Technology Operations or Modern Workplace leader from a larger corporate environment, looking for broader ownership and a role where you're closer to the people your technology supports.

Either way, you're a technologist at heart: curious, continually learning and technically credible, while increasingly focused on people and service leadership.

Education experience isn't essential.

You'll ideally bring:

  • Strong technology service delivery leadership experience
  • Practical ITSM experience across incident, request, problem and change
  • Experience leading and developing technical teams
  • Strong practical knowledge of Microsoft 365, endpoints, identity and Modern Workplace
  • Experience improving service through knowledge, self-service and automation
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • The technical depth to troubleshoot complex issues and challenge technical thinking
  • A leadership style that builds capability, accountability and trust

Next steps from here?

If your CV isn't completely up to date, don't worry. Just send through what you have.

Alternatively, contact Steven Fulop at xceltium on 0418 994 446 for a confidential discussion or send me a message on LinkedIn.

xceltium has been exclusively retained to manage this appointment. All direct applications and applications submitted through third parties will be referred to xceltium and managed as part of this recruitment process.

Every applicant will receive a response.

title: Facilities Technician I, II, III
description:
Grade 8 - 10

Non-Exempt

POSITION OVERVIEW

Performs intermediate skilled trades work maintaining, repairing, and troubleshooting a variety of facilities systems and Town equipment. Work performed involves diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining mechanical, electrical, structural, and other facility applicable components across all Town-owned facilities. Facility Mechanics may work on HVAC systems, lighting/fixtures, plumbing, traffic lights/signals, and other specialized building equipment/systems. Work is performed under minimal supervision.


Facilities Mechanic I position duties include, but are not limited to:

  • Knowledge & Safety: Working knowledge of preventative maintenance and basic repairs. Perform routine maintenance and inspections on variety of facility equipment, signs, and traffic signals. Diagnose and repair standard mechanical and electrical issues.
  • Manual/General Labor: Assists with minor electrical diagnosis and repairs. Responsible for ensuring clean Town equipment; maintain shop cleanliness. Includes water and wastewater treatment plant, pump stations and wells.
  • Equipment Operations: Familiarity with applicable diagnostic tools and equipment.
  • Administration/Compliance: Knowledge of policies related to facilities maintenance operations. Knowledge of occupational hazards and appropriate safety practices. Maintain accurate records of maintenance, parts usage, time, and materials.
  • Additional Tasks: Assists as needed to accomplish a variety of Facilities related tasks.

Facilities Mechanic II position duties include Level I duties in addition to, but not limited to:

  • Knowledge & Safety: Advanced mechanical knowledge and troubleshooting skills. Experience with diagnosing and repairing complex mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, and electrical issues in a wide variety of various facility equipment, signs, and traffic signals.
  • Manual/General Labor: Diagnose and repair various types of e specialty equipment including but not limited to traffic lights, signs, plumbing systems, etc. Inspect, repair, replace, and mount electrical components and fixtures. Perform specialized tasks such as HVAC diagnosis, treatment pumps and associated equipment.
  • Equipment Operations: Extensive experience with applicable diagnostic tools and equipment.
  • Administration/Compliance: Knowledge of policies related to facilities maintenance operations. Knowledge of occupational hazards and appropriate safety practices. Maintain accurate records of maintenance, parts usage, time, and materials.
  • Administrative: Assists in the training and mentoring of Mechanic I. Assist with facilities purchasing and disposal.

Facilities Mechanic III position duties include Level I and II duties in addition to, but not limited to:

  • Knowledge & Safety: Advanced mechanical knowledge and troubleshooting skills. Diagnoses and repairs major component systems of buildings, roofing systems, electrical panels, and high voltage 1ph/3ph systems, low voltage, three-phase, signposts and structural bases, traffic light systems, and complex computer-controlled systems. Additional knowledge of control wiring, VFD Programming, and troubleshooting.
  • Administration/Compliance: Develop and implement maintenance procedures and standards. Assists with the daily operations of the fleet maintenance department. Assists the Fleet & Facilities manager with facilities budget management and resources control. Coordinate cross-departmental facility’s needs. Negotiate with vendors and suppliers.
  • People Operations: May serve as the Team Lead.

title: VP, Strategic Accounts
description:
At ASAPP, our mission is simple: deliver the best AI-powered customer experience—faster than anyone else. To achieve that, we’re guided by principles that shape how we think, build, and execute. The Strategic Account Director is an individual contributor role that will be responsible for managing our growing business across a national territory but will have the opportunity to work on various initiatives. We are seeking an experienced, innovative sales professional to push the boundaries of AI and CX performance. Engage in growing existing customers and bringing in new logos.

The role is right for you if you are

  • Someone who can create a long-term, compelling vision and join the customer in partnership on their journey to solve their most significant challenges

  • Someone excited to create raving fans out of early adopters, risk takers & visionaries

  • Motivated by venturing into and believing in something to create a market that no one has invested in before

What you'll do

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to our customers, educating them on the contact center space, industry-specific adoption of AI and ML technologies, and overall methods of optimization for their business leveraging ASAPP

  • Act as a liaison for the customer internally, advocating for optimization of our product and process continuously identify creative strategies to engage customers and generate incremental value

  • Develop and execute a comprehensive account management strategy that is grounded in personalized research and a focused value hypothesis

  • Work closely with customers and channel partners to evangelize ASAPP and gain greater market adoption

  • Work on critical projects that increase our effectiveness across the customer lifecycle, from early business development through the steady-state (e.g., effective messaging, commercial positioning, time to value, optimized operations)

What you'll need

  • 10+ years exp selling enterprise SaaS

  • Extreme curiosity with a bias towards consultative, solution-oriented selling

  • Passionate about helping customers with transformative business outcomes and value

  • Solid understanding of Customer Service/Experience industry

  • Technical proficiency with advanced software technologies (eg AI)

  • High integrity and humility, leading to trust and credibility

  • Persistent follow-through driven by care

  • Positive attitude; finds ways to win and never quits

  • Tireless work ethic; operates with a sense of urgency at all times

  • Presumptive closer

What we'd like to see

  • Not “just” a product salesperson - you prioritize relationships and open dialogue to identify and provide solutions to a customer's needs. You are hyper-focused on the customer rather than the product being sold.

  • Showing up differently than a product vs. product seller - you do your research, ask the right questions, listen with the intent to meet the customer where they are & guide them to where they need to be

  • Knowledge of which resources to bring in & use the full force of the business and all of its assets

Benefits

  • Customer focused and ability to manage challenging priorities and to remain flexible and adaptable in stressful situations.

Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

As the Lead Analyst, Capital Finance, you will play a key role in managing capital investments that support this innovative network infrastructure while assisting with other key finance functions as needed. Acting as a trusted advisor to the North America Operations Leadership Team, you will ensure efficient capital allocation, identify risks and opportunities, and provide financial insights that drive value to the organization.

Work Location

Fully remote position open to candidates based anywhere in the U.S.

The Main Responsibilities

  • Capital Management: Partner with business and finance teams to ensure efficient capital allocation and investment management. Identify, assess, and manage risks and opportunities related to capital investments. Help shape the capital governance framework and processes to improve decision-making.
  • Financial Analysis & Reporting: Develop and maintain advanced financial models to support budgeting, forecasting, and investment decisions. Conduct monthly analysis and deliver readouts to stakeholders, including leadership and operational teams. Provide variance analysis and recommendations to key stakeholders.
  • Strategic Insights & Process Improvement: Synthesize complex data into clear, actionable insights using tools and techniques such as visual storytelling. Identify and implement process improvements to streamline workflows and drive efficiency. Organize and clarify ambiguous information to deliver accurate and insightful outputs.
  • Collaboration & Leadership: Build strong, collaborative relationships with stakeholders, including Corporate FP&A, Accounting, and Operations teams. Work cross-functionally to address reporting and operational needs, aligning stakeholders on key priorities. Take ownership of challenges, drive positive outcomes, and set a standard of excellence within the team.
  • Support a diverse portfolio of one-time projects and strategic initiatives, including reporting enhancements, new product launches, process optimization efforts, and cross-functional business initiatives.
  • Partner with business and technology teams to deliver system enhancements and development initiatives, resolving application defects, improving functionality, and ensuring solutions align with evolving business needs.

What We Look For in a Candidate

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in financial analysis, capital management, or a similar role.
  • Advanced skills in data analysis, financial modeling, and data visualization.
  • Exceptional problem-solving, decision-making, and communication skills.

title: Tool & Die Maker - Day Shift *$3,500 Sign On Bonus
description:
Tool & Die Maker - Day ShiftThe hours for the position are Monday - Thursday; 5:00am - 3:00pm


Since 1982, Sigma Engineered Solutions has been on an incredible journey. We started with just one plant in India and have expanded to 13 locations around the world. What began as a cost-effective supplier of low-voltage electrical products has grown into a global solutions provider of highly engineered, complex metal components, including machined parts and precision metal stampings.


At Sigma Engineered Solutions “your success is our mission.” It’s a promise we live by daily and it defines everything we do whether you are a team member or customer.


The Tool & Die Maker completes all assignments related to constructing, modifying, and conditioning multi-station metalworking dies. Fabricates new gauges, cutting and forming tools, and fixtures by applying comprehensive knowledge of tool and die design, machining, layout, assembly, and conditioning procedures.


What you will be doing:

Layout and Planning

  • Lay out work assignments of all complexity levels using verbal instructions, rough sketches, tooling, and product prints.
  • Visualize the completed product and determine required layout steps.

Measurement, Marking & Calculation

  • Compute dimensions and establish reference points, centerlines, and guidelines on tooling and product components.
  • Measure, mark, and scribe metal stock for machining with accuracy and precision.

Machining Operations

  • Determine necessary machining operations and perform machine setup.
  • Operate machine tools such as lathes, milling machines, and grinders to machine parts.
  • Verify conformance of machined parts to required specifications.

Assembly, Fitting & Finishing

  • Fit and assemble component parts into completed units or mechanisms.
  • Verify dimensions, alignment, and clearance of assembled parts.
  • Perform filing, stoning, grinding, scraping, and blending operations to ensure proper fit.
  • Use shims as needed to correct alignment or compensate for tolerance variations.

Die Setup, Testing & Inspection

  • Set dies in presses and perform trial operations to validate clearance, pressure performance, and ensure no binding occurs.
  • Inspect completed stamped parts to ensure adherence to engineering specifications.

Troubleshooting & Corrective Adjustments

  • Analyze and correct complex tool malfunctions in newly constructed or modified dies.
  • Verify dimensions, alignments, and clearances, and make adjustments or corrections to eliminate tolerance deviations in stamped products.

Tooling & Design Improvement

  • Recommend tooling design improvements—under engineering approval—to enhance tool life, product quality, production output, and to eliminate design-related issues.
  • Condition dies to prevent breakage of small or intricate tooling components.

Tools & Equipment Use

  • Utilize toolmakers’ hand tools and all related hand tools safely and effectively.
  • Operate precision measuring instruments including height gages, gage blocks, comparators, dial indicators, toolmakers’ microscopes, and micrometers to ensure parts meet specification and die stations are correctly aligned.

Heat-Treating Processes

  • Perform heat-treating procedures including hardening, stress relieving, and annealing tool steel.
  • Case-harden machine steel as necessary.

Training & Mentorship

  • Provide instruction and training to apprentices, trainees, and employees in lower classifications as required.

Other duties:

  • Follow safe work practices and keep the work area clean and organized.
  • Perform related duties as assigned.
  • Follow documented policies and procedures as designated by the company’s Employee Handbook and Local Work Rules. In addition, adhere to the proper Code of Conduct while on company property.

title: Salgsassistent til Q8 Lund, 25 timer
description:
Er du interesseret i en stilling, hvor du får mulighed for at tage ansvar, udvikle dig og gøre en reel forskel for kunderne? Så kan det være, at dit livs måske vigtigste job venter på dig her hos os. Seriøst!

Hos Q8 bliver du en del af et fællesskab, hvor vi passer på hinanden og sørger for, at du trives i dit arbejde. Når du har det godt, kan du give kunderne den bedste oplevelse – og det er præcis det, vi brænder for. Vores gode samarbejde internt er samtidig med til at drive den udvikling, vi som virksomhed er i fuld gang med. Q8 står nemlig midt i en spændende transformation, hvor vi arbejder aktivt med at reducere vores klimapåvirkning. Lyder det som noget for dig? Så bliv en del af Q8‑familien.

Hvad kommer du til at lave?

Som salgsassistent får du en hverdag, hvor ingen dage er ens. Du sørger for, at stationen altid er indbydende og klar til at tage imod kunderne. Det ene øjeblik hjælper du på forpladsen, det næste betjener du kunder ved kassen, tilbereder og serverer mad eller fylder varer op. Der er fart på – men også plads til grin med kollegaerne og tid til at give kunderne en god service.

Det praktiske

  • Ansættelsesform: timelønnet
  • Omfang: Ca. 25 timer pr. uge
  • Arbejdstid: Vagterne vil ligge både i hverdagene og weekenden, typisk i både dag –og aftentimerne.
  • Start: Efter aftale
  • Løn: Grundløn for ufaglærte: 142,17 kr. Grundløn for faglærte: 151,53 kr. Derudover får du aften-, nat-, weekend- og helligdagstillæg i henhold til butiksoverenskomsten.
  • Pension: 10,7% firmabetalt pension gennem PFA. Gælder efter 3 måneders ansættelse og for medarbejdere over 20 år – med mindre du allerede er omfattet af en pensionsordning, så får du pension fra start.

OBS! Du skal kunne fremvise en straffeattest, hvis du går videre i processen.

Hvad tilbyder vi dig?

  • En arbejdsplads med alsidige opgaver og mulighed for at lære nyt hver dag
  • Et stærkt fællesskab, hvor vi hjælper hinanden og har det sjovt
  • En medarbejderapp med mulighed for fleksibel lønudbetaling, indflydelse gennem vores ungeministerium samt gode fordele og rabatter
  • En struktureret onboardingproces, der sikrer, at du kommer godt fra start – understøttet af vores medarbejderapp, hvor du finder guides, træning og nyttige værktøjer

Hvis du vil vide mere om, hvordan det er at være medarbejder i Q8, så læs mere på karrierestationen.

Hvem passer jobbet til?

Vi leder efter dig, der har lyst til at tage ansvar og give kunderne en god oplevelse. Erfaring er ikke afgørende – det vigtigste er din energi og dit engagement.

OBS! For at søge skal du være fyldt 18 år og tale flydende dansk, da kundekontakt er en stor del af jobbet.

Klar på at blive en del af Q8?

I ansøgningen har du flere muligheder, men for at vi kan lære dig bedre at kende, så skal du besvare nogle enkelte spørgsmål. Derudover skal du optage en kort video, hvor du fortæller om dig selv og hvorfor du gerne vil arbejde hos Q8. Vi ved godt, at det kan lyde lidt grænseoverskridende, men det behøver ikke at være perfekt eller professionelt, og du kan bare filme på mobilen.

Du kan også vedhæfte dit CV, hvis du har et, men det er helt frivilligt. Vi håber at høre fra dig!

Det kan være dit livs måske vigtigste ansøgning - seriøst.

title: Tax Analyst II
description:
Purpose Statement: The Tax Analyst II is responsible for ensuring income tax compliance and reporting on a global basis for a rapidly growing multinational publicly traded company. This includes tax related issues such as preparation, planning and research as well as communicating with U.S. and non-U.S. finance teams. Expected to take on more complex responsibilities such as in-depth analysis and tax planning.

Key Job Accountabilities:

  • Responsible for timely preparation and support of the organization's various tax filings which may include both direct and indirect taxes.
  • Responsible for supporting tax management with maintaining the tax accounts. This will include maintaining schedules used to support the quarterly financial statements and tax footnotes in Plexus' 10Q's and 10K and/or statutory accounts.
  • Assist in the completion of tax reviews/audits by various taxing authorities. The audit process may include researching tax technical issues, understanding the underlying business process to determine the tax exposure and interacting with the auditor.
  • Assist in researching and documenting tax planning opportunities. This will include creating schedules and communicating with other individuals within the finance organization and creating schedules supporting the planning initiatives.
  • Assist in completing the monthly, quarterly and annual effective tax rate calculations for MEXGAAP. Assist in preparing and reviewing the monthly, quarterly and annual disclosures of tax information found in the financial statements. Assist in completing the annual effective tax rate calculations for USGAAP purposes.

Education/Experience Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 1 year of related experience; or equivalent work experience.
  • More than one (1) or more years of related experience is preferred.
  • A CPA designation (or equivalent) is preferred, but not required.
  • An equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the key job accountabilities may be considered.

Other Qualifications:

  • The employee must be self-motivated with the ability to follow through on assignments with little or no supervision.
  • The individual must possess the ability to work independently and in a team environment.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, attention to detail, research, analytical and organizational skills are paramount for the employee to successfully perform this position.
  • The individual must maintain objectivity and possess pro-active problem solving skills, along with the ability to make timely and effective recommendations to resolve problems as they arise.
  • The employee must keep all department, company and customer information they encounter during their employment confidential.
  • Google Workspace or Microsoft Word, Excel, tax research and preparation software.

Physical Requirements:

  • Professional office environment with suitable lighting, comfortable temperatures, and low noise level. May require prolonged periods of sitting at a desk, using a computer, and other office equipment. Minimal physical activity is generally involved, emphasizing the importance of good posture and ergonomic workplace arrangements.

Travel Requirements:

  • N/A

title: Electrical Construction Project Manager
description:

This is a hands-on position for someone who can take a project from the initial site visit or bid documents through estimating, proposal preparation, award, scheduling, construction, and closeout.


Our typical projects range from $25,000 to $500,000, although some projects are larger. Most are completed directly by LMI without the layers of coordination typically found on large, multi-trade construction projects.


Types of Projects


Projects may include:

  • Shopping center and parking lot lighting upgrades
  • Interior commercial and retail lighting
  • LED lighting conversions
  • Sports field and stadium lighting
  • Roadway and municipal lighting
  • Site lighting, pole installations, and underground electrical work
  • Lighting controls and related electrical improvements
  • Service upgrades, circuit replacements, and electrical infrastructure supporting lighting systems


Position Responsibilities


The person in this position will:


  • Review plans, specifications, scopes of work, and customer requirements
  • Conduct site visits and develop complete project scopes
  • Perform accurate labor, material, equipment, subcontractor, and production-cost estimates
  • Obtain vendor and subcontractor pricing when necessary
  • Prepare clear, detailed proposals, exclusions, qualifications, and alternates
  • Identify scope gaps, constructability issues, scheduling risks, and unusual project requirements before pricing

title: Data Engineer
description:
Data Engineer

  • Working Hours: Monday to Friday


At TTC, we are Enriching lives by connecting people and places.

For over 100 years, we’ve been bringing the world closer together by crafting journeys that create lasting memories, lifelong friendships and meaningful cultural connections. Across more than 70 countries and our award-winning brands, we design and deliver travel experiences that go beyond sightseeing - they change perspectives.

Behind every unforgettable journey is a passionate team making it happen. That’s where you come in.

  • Explore Beyond Boundaries. We are driven by curiosity.
  • Own the Outcome. We take responsibility for our decisions.

The Role

This is a chance to help build the modern data foundations behind TTC's growing Data and AI capability. You will design and develop reliable pipelines and trusted data products across customer, booking, digital, marketing, commercial and operational data, enabling analytics, data science and better decisions across our global portfolio of travel brands.

You will work in a modern Snowflake-based ecosystem alongside senior engineers, data scientists, analysts and data product colleagues, turning complex data into accessible, reusable, high-quality assets. The platform is being actively developed and scaled, so you will learn quickly, see your work used and grow alongside strong engineers who are happy to share what they know. If you care about doing things properly and want room to develop, you will do well here.


What Will You Do?

  • Build and maintain scalable, production-grade pipelines across customer, booking, digital, commercial and operational domains.
  • Turn raw data into trusted, reusable and well-modelled products for Analytics, Data Science and AI.
  • Develop solutions in Snowflake, SQL, Python and modern transformation tooling such as dbt.
  • Build analytical models that give consistent views of customers, bookings, products and key entities.
  • Implement automated testing, data quality controls, monitoring and observability across critical datasets.
  • Apply modern engineering practice including Git, code review, automated testing and CI/CD.
  • Monitor and optimise workloads for performance, scalability, resilience and cost.
  • Work with senior engineers to apply reusable patterns and technical standards.
  • Partner with Data Science, Insight and Data Product colleagues to translate needs into solid technical solutions.
  • Investigate data quality and pipeline issues, find root causes and fix them properly.


About You

Essential

  • Strong professional experience in data engineering or analytics engineering.
  • Strong hands-on capability with SQL and Python.
  • Experience with Snowflake or another modern cloud data platform.
  • Experience designing and developing ELT and ETL pipelines in production.
  • A good understanding of analytical and dimensional data modelling.
  • Experience with dbt or comparable modern transformation tooling.
  • Familiarity with Git, CI/CD, automated testing and data quality practice.
  • A collaborative mindset and a genuine interest in building things well.

Desirable

  • Experience with orchestration tools such as Airflow, Dagster, Prefect or Azure Data Factory.
  • Experience working within AWS, Azure, GCP or another enterprise cloud ecosystem.
  • Experience with complex customer, transactional, digital or behavioural data.
  • Exposure to data security, governance, lineage and documentation practice.
  • Curiosity about travel, hospitality or global consumer businesses.


Apply Now

If you want to build data foundations that thousands of colleagues and millions of travellers rely on, we would like to hear from you. Apply today, and tell us what you would want to build first.

academic alignment.

Work with the finance team to invoice and receive payments in a timely manner, and with the sales operations and enrollment teams to guide chaperones and families through pre-departure paperwork and learning.

Continuous Improvement: Debrief programs with schools and chaperones after they return home. Analize feedback survey data. Follow up on actionable items.

Strategic Initiatives: Leveraging your background and areas of expertise, support marketing, communication, networking, training, and other strategic projects to support the program line’s continued growth.

Reporting Excellence: Maintain accurate records of all sales activities and program statuses in our CRM system (e.g., Salesforce) and file management system in Microsoft Teams.

  • experience, with a proven track record of building strong client relationships.
  • Experience in international education or related K-12 industries. Experience working in or with secondary schools preferred.
  • Experience living, studying, or working abroad or in an intercultural space. Experience
  • designing or leading student travel programs preferred.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Understanding of budgets and price strategy.
  • Proficient with Microsoft products, Salesforce, and other CRM tools.
  • Willingness to be a flexible team player, with a passion for education and a belief in the power of global citizenship.
  • Willingness to travel for several domestic trips and one international trip per year to attend conferences, visit schools in person, join team trainings and events, and host one educator site visit.

title: Creative Ops Lead
description:
About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast — both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.

About the Role

The Design team at Polymarket is small, fast, and expected to punch well above its weight. We ship across paid social, lifecycle, partnerships, and brand with a lean roster of designers and motion talent, supplemented by freelancers and agency partners. The team moves at the speed of news cycles, which means the operational layer underneath creative production either works perfectly or everything grinds to a halt.

This is the role that makes the machine run. As Creative Ops Lead, you own the full creative pipeline: intake, briefing, prioritization, production, review, and delivery. You build and maintain the systems that let a small team ship at high volume without dropping quality or missing deadlines — and you close the loop between ad performance data and creative production so winning concepts get iterated and scaled in days, not weeks.

What You'll Do

  • Own the end-to-end creative pipeline across paid social, lifecycle, partnerships, and brand, running intake, briefing, prioritization, production, review, and delivery as one connected system

  • Build and maintain the operating infrastructure: briefs, trackers, asset libraries, naming conventions, and approval workflows that let the team ship at high volume without reinventing the wheel each campaign

  • Allocate designers, motion talent, and freelancers against the campaign calendar, matching capacity to demand and killing bottlenecks before they hit deadlines

  • Pull live ad performance data and route winning signals back into active briefs, ensuring top-performing concepts are iterated and scaled within days

  • Manage external production partners — staffing agencies, freelancers, and vendors — including sourcing, negotiating, onboarding, and holding quality bars throughout

  • Run compliance ops for league and partner creative, managing licensing guidelines, approval routing, and turnaround SLAs with external rights holders

  • Track and report on creative throughput, cycle times, and hit rates weekly, keeping the ops layer measurable and continuously improving

What We're Looking For

  • Proven end-to-end creative ops ownership at a growth company — you have built and run the full pipeline, not just managed parts of it

  • Direct experience building and managing creative workflows for paid social at scale, including briefing, production, and delivery across multiple concurrent campaigns

  • Track record sourcing, negotiating with, and managing freelance and agency partners, including holding quality bars under real deadline pressure

  • Clear experience closing the loop between ad performance data and creative production, with a process that moves from data signal to updated brief to live asset in days

  • Comfort managing compliance workflows with external rights holders, including approval routing and SLA tracking

  • Strong cross-functional instincts — you communicate with PMs and channel leads in terms of business impact and keep work moving without waiting to be unblocked

  • (Plus) Experience setting up DAMs and standing up creative automation tooling, including templated production, dynamic creative workflows, or AI-assisted generation

  • (Plus) Background in crypto, fintech, or a high-velocity consumer app where the pace of production is non-negotiable

Benefits

  • Competitive salary & equity

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage

  • 401k match

  • Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories

title: Senior Software Engineer, Data
description:
About us

Founded in 2017, Wayve is the leading developer of Embodied AI technology. Our advanced AI software and foundation models enable vehicles to perceive, understand, and navigate any complex environment, enhancing the usability and safety of automated driving systems.

Our vision is to create autonomy that propels the world forward. Our intelligent, mapless, and hardware-agnostic AI products are designed for automakers, accelerating the transition from assisted to automated driving. In our fast-paced environment big problems ignite us—we embrace uncertainty, leaning into complex challenges to unlock groundbreaking solutions. We aim high and stay humble in our pursuit of excellence, constantly learning and evolving as we pave the way for a smarter, safer future.

At Wayve, your contributions matter. We value diversity, embrace new perspectives, and foster an inclusive work environment; we back each other to deliver impact.

Make Wayve the experience that defines your career!

The role

Portal is the cloud platform that connects Wayve to the outside world: handling data exchange with partners, surfacing AI insights, and enabling the commercial deployment of Wayve's AI driver on vehicles across the globe.

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Data to help build Wayve's Data Transfer Hub: a mission-critical piece of infrastructure that will scale to transfer petabytes of sensor data per day from partners covering vehicles around the world.

This is a pivotal project at Wayve. You'll work as part of a small, high-autonomy team building a globally distributed hub-and-spoke data exchange system, working with partners like Uber, Stellantis and Nissan. Your work will help make Wayve's AI model training possible at scale.

Key responsibilities:

  • Build and operate large-scale data transfer pipelines for video, LiDAR and sensor data from global partners at up to PB/day scale
  • Contribute to the technical design of the Data Transfer Hub, making pragmatic trade-offs across UX, careliability, throughput, cost, partner constraints, observability and operational support
  • Build parallelised, distributed data transfer pipelines using Flyte for workflow orchestration, Kafka/event-driven patterns for lifecycle tracing, and Azure for storage and transfer infrastructure
  • Help implement and evolve a globally distributed hub-and-spoke data transfer model to retrieve and share sensor data at scale with partners
  • Write infrastructure-as-code in Terraform and pipeline logic primarily in Python
  • Build reliable operational foundations, including retry strategies, backfills, data integrity checks, lifecycle/state tracking, dashboards and alerting
  • Work on cloud-to-cloud and cross-cloud networking solutions, with Azure as the primary cloud platform
  • Once established, participate in an out-of-hours on-call and support rotation.
  • Collaborate with product, commercial and partner-facing teams to understand constraints and deliver solutions that solve real customer and partner problems
  • Work in a fast-changing environment where requirements and partner deliverable dates evolve, while maintaining high engineering standards

About you

In order to set you up for success as a Senior Software Engineer at Wayve, we’re looking for the following skills and experience.

Essential

  • Proven experience building and operating large-scale data transfer, ingestion or data processing pipelines, ideally at multi-TB or PB scale
  • Strong software engineering skills
  • Experience delivering & maintaining production systems
  • Experience with workflow orchestration for parallelised jobs; Flyte preferred, but Airflow, Prefect or similar tools are also relevant
  • Experience building reliable, observable data systems, including retry strategies, backfills, data integrity checks, lifecycle/state tracking and operational alerting
  • Strong cloud platform skills, with Azure preferred; experience with AWS or GCP is a plus
  • Proficiency in Python and Terraform
  • Experience with blob/object storage, large-scale file movement, networking or cloud-to-cloud data transfer
  • A product mindset: you think about the customer and build solutions that fix real problems, not just implement requirements
  • Comfort working in a fast-changing environment with evolving requirements
  • A strong sense of ownership: you take responsibility for outcomes, communicate clearly, and help the team move quickly

Desirable

  • Experience working with external data partners or customer-facing technical integrations
  • Background in autonomous vehicles, robotics, geospatial data, video processing or other data-intensive domains
  • Experience with Kafka or other event-driven systems for transfer observability and lifecycle tracking
  • Experience building dashboards to communicate transfer job status
  • Multi-cloud experience across Azure, AWS and/or GCP
  • Experience improving cost efficiency, throughput or reliability of large-scale cloud data systems

This is a full-time role based in our office in London. At Wayve we want the best of all worlds so we operate a hybrid working policy that combines time together in our offices and workshops to fuel innovation, culture, relationships and learning, and time spent working from home.

Wayve is committed to creating an inclusive interview experience. If you require any accommodations or adjustments to participate fully in our interview process, please let us know.

We understand that everyone has a unique set of skills and experiences and that not everyone will meet all of the requirements listed above. If you’re passionate about self-driving cars and think you have what it takes to make a positive impact on the world, we encourage you to apply.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

For US candidates only, please visit E-Verify Notice and Participation and Right to Work

title: Member of Technical Staff, GPU Compiler
description:
At SF Tensor, we're building the future of high-performance compute

We firmly believe that the future of AI depends on the unglamorous: rethinking and rebuilding the stack, all the way down. From the hardware underneath it to the compiler targeting it and the cloud running it. Right now those three things fight each other and that friction shows up as a tax on every researcher trying to build something ambitious. We're here to axe that tax and make compute faster, cheaper and more available. When we succeed, compute will be portable enough that "which cloud, which chip" stop being something you worry about.

To achieve this, we are building our Kernel Optimizer, which takes code and finds its fastest possible form for whatever vendor and cluster topology you point it at, automatically, as well as the Model Foundry which manages the runs, makes research easier and moves workloads across clouds and chips as prices and availability ship, instead of leaving you locked into whatever vendor you signed with first.

We're backed by Susa Ventures, Y Combinator, along with some great funds and angels including Max Mullen and Paul Graham, as well as founders and executives at Neuralink, Notion and AMD. We're looking for researchers, engineers and organizations who agree with the basic premise: you don't get the next leap in AI without a leap in compute first.

About the Role

We build the fastest GPU compiler in the world. Most compilers have to preserve correctness at every transform, constraining how far they can search, while we prove correctness at the end instead, allowing us to search a far wider space, with agents, with RL, with anything that works and still guarantee the result. It's why we hold #1 on NVIDIA's own kernel benchmark across hundreds of production kernels.

We're hiring a Member of Technical Staff for GPU Compiler Engineering to build the machine that does the searching.

You'll be working on the entire pipeline end to end (StableHLO ingestion, MLIR dialects & passes, backend code generation, executable GPU & host binaries). The pipeline already does things worth seeing. Given only a naive attention spec, the search found FlashAttention v4-level performance on a B300 in about 25 minutes and your job will be to make sure that next time, we beat FlashAttention with ease.

You'll have access to better tooling than anywhere else because we own the stack all the way down to the ISA, allowing us to create kernels that others can't even express. For example, our custom LLVM backend emits cubins directly, without ptxas, letting us work on instruction selection, scheduling, register allocation and stall counts. Our team understands the hardware better than anyone else, to this extent we've built a bit-exact software model of Blackwell's tcgen05.

You'll be writing kernels that ship immediately on runs such as pre-training AlphaFold v3 at 3.4× the throughput, post-training robotics models on Trainium or running our custom RL rollout engine on TPU at multi-100B parameter scale.

What You'll Do

  • You'll build and extend MLIR dialects and passes to optimize training and inference workloads

  • You'll work in our LLVM backend, below ptxas, on instruction selection, scheduling, register allocation and direct cubin emission and work on standing up equivalent depth on AMD, TPU and Trainium targets

  • You'll expand our search-based compiler infrastructure, including agent- and RL-driven program search and the formal correctness proofs that make aggressive search safe

  • You'll implement classic compiler optimizations tuned for large-scale training

  • You'll create hybrid codegen paths for cases where direct MLIR lowering isn't practical

  • You'll own testing, benchmarking and performance regression systems, including bit-identical hardware models

  • You'll work closely with our research team and with customer workloads to find the optimization opportunities that matter

What We're Looking For

  • Someone with deep experience in compiler infrastructure (LLVM, MLIR or similar)

  • Someone with a strong background in GPU architecture and low-level optimization (CUDA, ROCm or similar)

  • Someone with hands-on experience with at least one of: PTX/SASS, GCN/RDNA assembly or other GPU ISAs

  • Someone familiar with ML compiler stacks (XLA, TVM, Triton, torch.compiler or similar)

  • Someone with solid systems programming skills in C++ and/or Rust

  • Someone with a proven track record of building production-grade compiler infrastructure

Nice to Have

  • Someone with experience in autotuning or search-based optimization

  • Someone with a background in formal verification, proof assistants or SMT solvers

  • Someone with experience writing or maintaining an LLVM backend

  • Someone with a background in distributed systems or multi-device compilation

  • Someone who's contributed to open-source compiler projects

  • Someone familiar with large-scale training infrastructure

  • Someone with experience in (Stable)HLO

Why Join Us

Most compiler engineers spend their career inside a constraint they didn't choose, forced to ensure that every transform is correct on it's own. If you've ever wanted to put real search inside a compiler and never had the architectural freedom or the hardware budget to try it, this is the job for you. This is a chance to work at the very bottom of the stack on a compiler that is already the fastest in the world, with a direct and measurable effect on the cost of every large training run we touch.

We're a small team operating at frontier scale. We pre-trained foundation models on 4,000 AMD GPUs as a team of three, designed and brought up GB300 NVL72 clusters and designed a TOP500 supercomputer.

We believe that hard problems get solved in person and most of our work happens at our office in San Francisco. We offer relocation assistance and, where possible, we'd like you here as often as possible.

The base salary range for this full-time position is $285,000-$315,000, plus meaningful equity and benefits.

title: Software Engineer, GTM
description:
Half the people who call themselves GTM engineers have never shipped production code. This job is for the other half.

The Reality

This is a software engineering role that happens to point straight at revenue. You'll write and ship production code, own the systems you build, and be measured by whether the revenue engine runs better because of your work. If your background is engineering that never got to touch the business, this is the role where it finally does. If it's been RevOps where you were quietly the most technical person in the org and nobody ever let you build properly, same.

We're in the office five days a week in San Francisco. A company moving this fast catches its own mistakes sooner with the whole team in one room, thinking out loud at a whiteboard.

This will probably be one of the harder jobs you've had. It should also be one of the more interesting ones, because the revenue problems you'll be solving here will be the catalyst for our continued hyper growth.

Sound exciting? Good, we are too :)

What We're Building

Hyperbound is the Revenue Activation Platform and agentic operating system for sales, built across Hyperbound Practice (AI roleplay), Hyperbound Perform (real call scoring and coaching), and Kota, our AI agent that acts on what we find. We don't just record what happens on a call, we change what happens next.

Founded in 2023 out of YC (S23), we're around 45 people now, Series A, $18M raised total. Last quarter we doubled headcount, revenue nearly doubled with it, and net revenue retention landed above 300%. Teams at LinkedIn, Workday, Vanta, and Intel run their sales orgs on us.

The Role

You'll build the systems the go-to-market org runs on: lead routing and enrichment, pipeline and forecasting tooling, scoring and deal-desk workflows, and the data layer that ties it all into one source of truth. This is production engineering: services and code you own, integrated across our CRM, product, and billing data, built to hold up as we scale. Where a no-code tool is genuinely the right call, use it; the bar is that you can build the real thing when that's what the job needs.

There's a part of this job most GTM engineers never get. You'll dogfood Hyperbound on Hyperbound: our own reps run on Practice, Perform, and Kota, so the internal systems you build plug straight into the product we sell, and what you learn building them feeds back into the roadmap. You'll work closely with the founders and GTM leadership, act as part engineer and part systems designer for the revenue org, and have real say in what we build, not just how.

The Team

We're assembling a cracked team of builders, operators, and people who close. We've hired from our competition, brought on former founders, and pulled in early customers who loved the product enough to come build it.

The engineers here are builders first. Some have started their own companies. Nobody is precious about their code, and nobody hides behind "not my team's problem"; people see something broken and fix it. Someone is usually demoing something they shipped that morning, and the whiteboards get erased and rewritten all day. You can feel it when a team actually believes in what it's building, and that's very real here. It's also not a mattress-under-your-desk startup: plenty of people have kids, people leave to make dinner, and they come back the next morning and ship. High standards don't require burnout.

We've doubled in size since this photo was taken a few months ago

When we close a real milestone we celebrate for real; after our Series A we took the whole team to Bali.

Ownership and Equity

You own the outcome end to end: the systems you build, the revenue they move, and everything that happens after they ship. No process shields you from the responsibility, and none of it shields you from the credit either. Equity here is real, with real secondary opportunities, and we want the people who build this early to end up meaningfully rewarded for it.

Compensation and Benefits

Compensation: $160K-$200K+ based on experience + equity

Benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401k

Unlimited PTO

Commuter benefits

Paid lunch and dinner in the office

The Interview Process

We move fast: an intro call, a technical conversation with a build component alongside the people you'd actually work with, and a final conversation with the founders. We've closed roles in as little as one to two weeks when it's the right fit on both sides.

Equal Opportunity

Hyperbound is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, and we don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
